Business Partnership and Problem Definition

Build trusted relationships with business leaders, functional teams, and subject matter experts to understand priorities, operating context, constraints, and decision needs.

Lead discovery sessions to frame ambiguous business challenges, identify root causes, define hypotheses, and determine where analytics or data science can create meaningful value.

Translate business needs into clear problem statements, success measures, business requirements, user stories, and analytical plans.

Challenge requests when the proposed solution does not address the underlying business problem and recommend a more effective approach.

Align stakeholders on scope, priorities, assumptions, dependencies, risks, and expected outcomes before development begins.

Analytics and Data Science Delivery

· Own end-to-end analytics and data science initiatives from discovery and data assessment through modeling, validation, implementation, adoption, and outcome measurement.

· Analyze large and complex datasets to identify patterns, drivers, anomalies, opportunities, and actionable insights.

· Design, develop, and evaluate statistical, predictive, and machine learning solutions using methods appropriate to the business question.

· Define evaluation criteria that include analytical performance, interpretability, operational feasibility, business impact, and risk.

· Perform data profiling, cleansing, reconciliation, and validation to ensure analytical outputs are accurate, explainable, and fit for purpose.

· Develop decision-support tools, analyses, dashboards, and prototypes using SQL, Python, R, Power BI, Excel, or related tools.

Insight Communication and Influence

Synthesize complex analysis into clear business narratives, options, recommendations, and implications for executive and non-technical audiences.

Create effective visualizations and presentations that focus on decisions, business impact, tradeoffs, and recommended actions rather than technical detail alone.

Facilitate stakeholder reviews, resolve conflicting perspectives, and influence decisions using evidence and sound business judgment.

Communicate limitations, assumptions, uncertainty, and risks transparently so stakeholders can make informed decisions.

Partner with users to validate outputs, incorporate feedback, drive adoption, and confirm that delivered solutions address the intended business need.

Delivery Leadership and Cross-Functional Collaboration

Manage analytical backlogs, priorities, user stories, acceptance criteria, and delivery progress in Azure DevOps within an Agile environment.

Coordinate with data engineering, application, product, and platform teams on data availability, solution design, implementation, and production readiness.

Provide analytical leadership without assuming primary ownership for backend platform engineering, pipelines, or infrastructure.

Mentor Data Scientists and Analysts in business problem framing, stakeholder engagement, analytical rigor, documentation, and insight communication.

Establish and promote best practices for reproducibility, model validation, documentation, governance, and responsible use of data and analytics.

Identify opportunities to improve processes, reporting, decision workflows, and the organization’s broader analytics maturity.

description:
Do you enjoy spreadsheets, analyzing information, solving problems, and figuring out the most efficient way to accomplish something?




Royal Maintenance Group is a fast-growing national contracting and property services company operating across 27 states, and we're looking for a highly analytical person to join our team.




You do not need previous estimating or industry experience.




We are specifically interested in candidates with backgrounds or strong interests in areas such as:

MathematicsAccountingFinanceComputer ScienceEngineeringEconomicsData AnalyticsBusiness Analytics


What Will You Actually Be Doing?




Your job will be to help us figure out what projects should cost.

Our company manages large commercial projects throughout the country. Before we can price a project for a customer, someone needs to analyze the property, determine what resources will be required, calculate costs, and make sure the project can be completed profitably.

That's where you come in.




You will analyze information such as:

Property sizes and measurementsLabor requirementsMaterial costsEquipment requirementsVendor and subcontractor pricingMaps and property layoutsHistorical project dataProject specificationsProfit marginsCustomer requirements


You'll then use that information to build accurate estimates and pricing models.

Think of the position as a combination of math, business analysis, problem solving, and project strategy.




What We're Looking For:

We care much more about how you think than whether you've worked in our industry before.




You may be a great fit if:

You're naturally good with numbersYou're extremely detail-orientedYou enjoy solving complicated problemsYou're very comfortable using computersYou're strong with Excel or spreadsheetsYou can look at a lot of information and make sense of itYou notice details other people missYou learn new systems quicklyYou're organizedYou're comfortable making decisionsYou take ownership of your workYou're ambitious and want to grow


Previous estimating or construction experience is NOT required.

We will teach you our industries and how our projects work.

We're looking for someone who can bring the analytical ability.




The Projects:

You'll work on pricing projects for major commercial properties throughout the United States.

Depending on the season and division, projects may involve:

Snow and ice managementCommercial roofingProperty maintenanceFacility servicesOther commercial contracting services


One day you might be analyzing the cost to service a portfolio of commercial properties during a snowstorm. Another day you might be speaking with subcontractors executing the operations.

The industries change.




The underlying job is the same: analyze the project, understand the numbers, and determine what it should cost.

$80,000 per year

Full-time position.

Monday through Friday

8:00 AM – 4:00 PM

Hoboken Office

1 Newark Street

Hoboken, NJ 07030




Our office is located just steps from the Hoboken PATH station, making it extremely convenient from Manhattan and throughout North Jersey.

No Industry Experience? That's Okay.

We're not necessarily looking for someone who already knows our business.

We're looking for someone who is smart, analytical, curious, and capable of learning it.

You'll get exposure to how a large national company prices projects, evaluates profitability, manages vendors, makes operational decisions, and grows into new markets.




Career Growth

We're looking for someone who can eventually become much more than an entry-level analyst.

As you learn the business and demonstrate your abilities, there may be opportunities to advance into:

Senior EstimatingBusiness AnalyticsPricing StrategyProject ManagementOperationsDivision ManagementSenior Management


Royal Maintenance Group is continuing to expand, and we want ambitious people who are interested in growing alongside the company.

HOW TO APPLY

The Standardized Organoid Model Center is an NIH-funded initiative dedicated to advancing organoid research through the development of validated, reproducible, and well-characterized organoid models. description:
Are you ready to harness multi-omics, comparative genomics, and agentic AI to accelerate vaccines and immune therapies from discovery to the clinic? In this role, you will transform complex human and pathogen datasets into clear, decision-driving insights that shape antigen design, patient stratification, and translational strategy across high-priority programs.



Based in Cambridge, MA you will work in a collaborative, multidisciplinary environment alongside immunologists, molecular biologists, and data scientists. If you thrive at the intersection of computation and experiment—designing reproducible pipelines on HPC and cloud platforms while partnering closely with the lab to iterate rapidly—this role offers the opportunity to influence study design, guide go/no-go decisions, and help advance novel immune-based therapies toward patients.



Accountabilities

You will design, implement, and deliver robust analyses across genomics, bulk and single-cell transcriptomics, and multi-omics to answer program-critical questions with statistical rigor. You will assemble genomes, call variants, and perform comparative genomics and phylogenetic analyses on bacterial and viral pathogens to inform antigen selection and surveillance strategy.You will apply machine learning and statistical modeling to discover biomarkers, stratify patients, predict antigen immunogenicity, and forecast treatment response, translating model outputs into actionable program recommendations. You will also build, optimize, and maintain reproducible workflows using HPC schedulers and AWS to scale analyses, reduce turnaround time, and ensure traceability.

In addition, you will design and integrate LLM-powered agentic workflows for literature mining, data extraction, and pipeline orchestration to accelerate discovery and improve developer productivity. Working closely with experimental scientists, you will propose computationally informed experiments, interpret results, and refine study designs to improve confidence and reduce cycle time.

You will generate translational insights through differential expression, pathway enrichment, and functional annotation, connecting molecular signals to biological mechanisms and clinical hypotheses. You will produce publication-quality visualizations and reports, present findings clearly to cross-functional stakeholders, and champion version control, workflow managers, and reproducible research practices to strengthen code quality and method sharing across programs.



Finally, you will stay current with emerging tools in bioinformatics, AI/ML, and agentic AI, piloting new approaches, sharing learnings, and scaling successful methods across the portfolio.



Essential Skills and Experience

You should have a PhD in Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Genomics, Molecular Biology, Computer Science, or a closely related quantitative discipline, with 2–5 years of industry experience.Alternatively, you may have an MS in a relevant discipline with 4–6 years of industry experience in bioinformatics, computational biology, or genomics.A demonstrated track record of independent research through publications, conference presentations, or successful project delivery is expected.You should bring proficiency in R and/or Python for genomic data analysis, statistical computing, and data visualization, including tools such as ggplot2, Bioconductor, tidyverse, pandas, and scikit-learn.Hands-on experience with NGS data analysis is required, including alignment tools such as STAR, BWA, and Bowtie2; quantification tools such as Salmon, featureCounts, and HTSeq; and variant calling tools such as GATK and bcftools.You should be familiar with RNA-seq analysis workflows, including differential expression methods such as DESeq2, edgeR, and limma, as well as pathway analysis and gene set enrichment approaches such as ssGSEA and MSigDB. description:
Bioinformatics Scientist is a remote review track for evaluating AI outputs across research science reasoning, calculations, and research workflows. Reviewers grade derivations and assumptions, reproduce key results, and document the correct method so the modeling team can train on it.


  Why this role matters
 Research science models live or die on whether their derivations actually hold up under scrutiny. AuraOne uses scientific specialists to grade outputs the way a peer reviewer would — checking assumptions, reproducing key steps, and capturing the right method alongside the wrong one.


  Responsibilities
 
  Review AI outputs against current research science methods, conventions, and prior work for Bioinformatics Scientist assignments.
  Reproduce or sanity-check key derivations, calculations, or experimental claims.
  Flag dimensional, methodological, and citation errors with structured severity tags.
  Capture the corrected reasoning or worked example so the modeling team can train on it.
  Adjudicate disputed answers against textbooks, papers, or community standards.
  Maintain reviewer-quality scores in inter-rater calibration cycles.
 
  Qualifications
 
  Graduate-level training or equivalent applied experience in research science or a closely related field for Bioinformatics Scientist work.
  Hands-on experience publishing, teaching, or advising on the topic at a professional level.
  Comfort applying multi-page rubrics consistently across long batches.
  Clear written reasoning that cites methods, papers, or worked examples.
  Reliable async availability for at least 10 hours per week.
 
  Example tasks
 
  Reproduce a research science derivation from a model output and flag any algebraic or dimensional errors.
  Grade a model's literature summary against the cited papers and rate the citation quality.
  Adjudicate a disputed answer between two reviewers using textbook methods.
  Audit a 25-row batch for rubric consistency and report drift to the program lead.
 
  Nice to have
 
  PhD, postdoc, or industry research experience in the topic area.
  Prior work reviewing AI-assisted research tooling and its failure modes.
  Multilingual fluency for non-English papers and corpora.
 
  Skills

 Remote — US-eligible. Remote · Independent specialist contractor. Employment type: CONTRACTOR. Applicants must be authorized to work from US.

title: Robotics Engineer
description:
JOB SUMMARY The Robotics Engineer develops, programs, integrates, commissions, and troubleshoots industrial robotic systems used in custom automated machinery. This position integrates robots with machine controls, safety systems, peripheral equipment, and end-of-arm tooling while ensuring each application meets Altron and customer requirements for safety, quality, performance, and documentation. The role works with Controls Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Assembly, Program Management, and customers throughout design, build, runoff, installation, and field support.


ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS
Robot Programming and Integration

Develop, modify, test, and optimize robot programs using teach pendants and three-dimensional offline simulation software.
Set up, configure, and commission industrial robots, including Fanuc, Yaskawa Motoman, KUKA, and similar platforms.
Configure and troubleshoot communication between robots, programmable logic controllers, safety systems, and peripheral equipment.
Develop and support robotic applications including material handling, dispensing, routing, welding, and other automated processes.
Define end-of-arm tooling requirements and support tooling selection, setup, integration, testing, and troubleshooting.
Verify robot hardware installation and coordinate corrective action with Controls Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, and Assembly as needed.

Commissioning, Debug, Installation, and Customer Support:

Debug and troubleshoot robot programs, communications, safety functions, process equipment, and application performance.
Validate robotic safety systems and confirm compliance with applicable company, customer, and industry requirements.
Confirm that robotic applications meet customer specifications, quality expectations, process requirements, and acceptance criteria.
Support machine runoff, installation, startup, and field service activities at Altron and customer facilities.
Travel up to 50% as required to support installations, startups, customer service, and other project needs, both domestically and internationally.
Conduct operator and maintenance training when required.
Communicate project status, technical concerns, and required corrective actions to the appropriate internal and customer contacts.

Technical Collaboration and Documentation:

Read and interpret mechanical drawings, electrical schematics, controls documentation, and robot-to-PLC interfaces.
Collaborate with Controls Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Assembly, Program Management, customers, and vendors throughout project execution.
Prepare and maintain robot software, operating procedures, setup information, and safety documentation.
Assist with electrical and mechanical activities when needed to support project schedules and successful system integration.
Participate in continuous improvement, quality, and workplace safety activities.
Perform other duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS

Associate degree in automation technology, robotics, mechatronics, electrical engineering technology, or a related field required; bachelor's degree in an engineering discipline preferred.
One to five years of experience in industrial robotics, automation integration, robot programming, or a related field preferred.
Experience with Fanuc, Yaskawa Motoman, KUKA, or similar industrial robot platforms.
Familiarity with robotic material handling, dispensing, routing, welding, or similar applications.
Working knowledge of robot programming, teach pendants, offline simulation software, robot communications, and machine-control practices.
Ability to read and interpret mechanical drawings, electrical schematics, and controls documentation.
Strong mechanical aptitude and the ability to understand automated machine operation and end-of-arm tooling requirements.
Strong troubleshooting, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
Computer literacy, including proficiency with Microsoft Office and the ability to learn required engineering and programming software.
Strong verbal and written communication skills, with technical writing skills preferred.
Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced and changing environment.
Self-motivated and able to work effectively both independently and within cross-functional teams.
Flexibility to work additional or nonstandard hours as project, installation, and customer requirements dictate.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

Competitive compensation

401(k) plan with company match
Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP)
Paid time off and paid holidays
Company-paid life insurance
Short-term and long-term disability insurance
Employee Assistance Program
Tuition reimbursement and professional development opportunities, when applicable

description: Robotics Engineer  We are building one of the most potentially consequential companies of the century. Our mission is to accelerate the world's transition to fusion energy while safeguarding humankind. This is not a normal company. This is not a normal job. We are committed for the long term to win.  We're looking for robotics engineers to stand up and grow Fuse's robotic manufacturing capability from the ground up. You will design, build, program, and deploy robotic cells that handle the full lifecycle of our pulsed-power hardware, from individual components up to our complete Impedance-Matched Marx Generator (IMG) modules. This is a hands-on, high-responsibility role: you'll select the robots, design the end-effectors and fixturing, write the control and vision software, integrate everything into a working line, and keep it running. You'll work shoulder to shoulder with our pulsed-power, mechanical, and electrical engineers to make our hardware manufacturable by robots.  What We Value   Obsess about the details — sloppy work costs us later, so do it right the first time.  Care — pick up the trash. Do things no one asks you to do. Go the extra mile because you care.  Act with urgency — every hour matters more than it feels like it does.  Be responsible for the outcome, not just the task; if it is not working, it remains your problem until it is fixed.  Assume good intent — disagree openly, then commit fully once a call is made. Build automated assembly, fastening, bonding, alignment, and handling processes for high-voltage, high-energy parts, including heavy and delicate components. Design and fabricate custom end-effectors, grippers, tooling, and fixtures tailored to our components. Program and integrate industrial and/or collaborative robots (arms, gantries, mobile platforms) with PLCs, motion controllers, and factory software. Background in pulsed power, Marx generators, capacitors, high-voltage systems, or fusion/plasma hardware. Experience with mobile robots or automated maintenance/inspection in field environments.  Experience standing up a new automation function or production line. Comfortable working hands-on in a lab and production environment around high-voltage and high-energy equipment, following strict safety procedures.  Ability to lift and maneuver equipment and tooling as needed during cell build-out and maintenance.  Occasional travel to other Fuse locations.    Benefits   Medical, dental, and vision coverage.  Relocation assistance for roles that require it.  Flexible time off. At Loombotic, we’re automating wire harness manufacturing.


We need an exceptional robotics engineer to make robots assemble harnesses reliably. You’ll focus on robot and end-effector programming, machine vision and manipulation.


The work is physical and unforgiving: finding a small contact, handling a flexible wire, aligning it with a connector and inserting it correctly. Then knowing whether it worked, recovering when it didn’t and doing it thousands of times.


You’ll own the software that connects perception to action: camera calibration, visual localization, motion, end-effector control and verification. You’ll work closely with our mechatronics team to improve the hardware and software together.


We have 20,000 square feet of factory to automate, with a goal of producing hundreds of thousands of harnesses per month by mid-2027.


You should be comfortable moving between code, cameras and real hardware, and staying with a problem until the machine works consistently.


We use AI agents wherever they make engineering better.

description:
Alliance Automation began operations in August 2008, seizing an opportunity to provide automation solutions to underserved industries. Our innovative thinkers design and build robotic automation systems that optimize production processes. We provide automation solutions for a multitude of industries; each helping upgrade efficiency, increase throughput and guarantee reliability in production.

Job Description:

POSITION OVERVIEW

Alliance Automation is seeking a Robotics Engineer to design, program, commission, and 

support industrial robotic systems used in custom automation equipment.

This position is intended for an automation professional with strong hands-on robotic

programming, integration, troubleshooting, and commissioning experience. The Robotics 

Engineer will take technical ownership of robotic applications while working closely with Controls 

Engineers, Mechanical and Electrical Designers, Machine Assembly, Applications, Project 

Management, and customers.

The Robotics Engineer supports projects from concept and simulation through programming, 

integration, runoff, installation, and customer acceptance. This position is expected to remain 

hands-on and capable of solving difficult robotic application and integration problems both at 

Alliance Automation and at customer facilities.

TOP 5 RESPONSIBILITIES

Robot Programming and Commissioning

Program, configure, commission, and troubleshoot industrial robotic systems for material handling, machine tending, assembly, dispensing, welding, palletizing, vision-guided applications, and other automated processes.

Robotic System Integration

Integrate robots with PLC/PAC systems, machine controls, safety systems, vision systems, end-of-arm tooling, servo equipment, industrial networks, and other automation components.

Application Development and Optimization

Develop robot programs, motion strategies, frames, payload configurations, recovery routines, and application-specific logic. Optimize robot motion, cycle time, reliability, and overall system performance.

Technical Project Execution

Support robotic applications from concept through customer acceptance. Identify technical risks, assist with project planning, support machine integration, and help projects meet performance, schedule, and customer requirements.

Standards, Support, and Knowledge Sharing

Develop and improve robotic programming standards, reusable routines, documentation, troubleshooting practices, and commissioning methods. Share robotic knowledge with Controls Engineers and technicians to increase the overall robotics capability of Alliance Automation.

ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES / DUTIES

Program and commission industrial robots and associated automation equipment.

Develop robot programs, frames, tool data, payloads, motion paths, I/O interfaces, and recovery routines.

Configure and integrate robot controllers with PLC/PAC systems and industrial networks.

Integrate robot safety functions with machine safety systems and applicable safety devices.

Configure and support robot-based and external machine-vision applications.

Support end-of-arm tooling development, integration, setup, and troubleshooting.

Optimize robot paths, motion parameters, cycle time, and application performance.

Develop safe and effective automatic recovery and fault-handling strategies.

Conduct robotic application reviews and identify potential technical risks before build and commissioning.

Support robot simulation, reach studies, cycle-time analysis, and application feasibility when required.

Assist Controls Engineers with robotic integration and troubleshooting.

Lead troubleshooting and root-cause analysis of difficult robotic and automation issues.

Support Applications with robotic concepts, technology selection, feasibility reviews, quotations, and labor estimates.

Participate in machine runoff, installation, commissioning, training, and customer acceptance.

Develop and maintain robotic programming standards, templates, documentation, and reusable solutions.

Provide technical guidance and knowledge sharing to engineers and technicians.

Travel to customer facilities for installation, commissioning, troubleshooting, training, and production support.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS/EXPERIENCE

Five or more years of industrial robotics, controls, or automation experience preferred.

Related engineering or technical degree, or equivalent technical education and work experience.

Advanced programming and troubleshooting capability with at least one major industrial robot platform.

Experience with FANUC, Yaskawa, ABB, Kawasaki, KUKA, or similar industrial robotic systems.

Strong understanding of robotic motion, coordinate systems, frames, payloads, tooling, I/O, and application programming.

Experience integrating robots with PLC/PAC systems and industrial networks.

Working knowledge of machine safety and robotic safety systems.

Experience with machine vision, vision-guided robotics, or robotic inspection applications preferred.

Experience with servo systems, end-of-arm tooling, and other automation equipment preferred.

Ability to diagnose complex robotic, electrical, controls, and process-related problems.

Ability to estimate robotic programming, commissioning, and site-support labor requirements.

Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and root-cause problem-solving skills.

Ability to communicate technical information clearly to engineers, customers, leadership, and other departments.

Willingness to remain hands-on with programming, commissioning, troubleshooting, and field support.

Ability to adapt to shifting priorities and travel to customer facilities as required.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

A successful Robotics Engineer does more than program robots.

This person takes ownership of robotic applications, develops reliable and maintainable solutions, reduces commissioning time, improves cycle time and equipment performance, identifies technical risks before they become project problems, and helps increase the robotics capability of the entire Controls Engineering team.

The result is robotic systems that are safe, reliable, maintainable, efficient, and ready to perform in production.

We are looking for a Robotics AI Strategy & Program Lead who can own end-to-end, cross-functional

initiatives that cut across AI research, robotics engineering, data infrastructure, and manufacturing

operations. They will be known as an operator who gets things done across complex organizations.

This role blends strategy, program management, analytics, and hands-on AI tools work: you will

structure the problems, build the dashboards, dive into the data, leverage and build AI agents, and drive

large programs to completion while unblocking teams across IT, Purchasing, Vendors, Finance, HR, and

Manufacturing.

You will be embedded with AI researchers, roboticists, AI engineers, data engineers, and AI product

managers, translating between technical and non-technical stakeholders and ensuring that what we

build is strategic, measurable, and shippable - from fast-turnaround experiments to multi-year platform

bets.

What you will own

Program and project leadership

• Own end-to-end cross-functional projects from problem framing and strategy through

execution, measurement, and iteration.

• Program manage large, multi-team initiatives (e.g., new robotics AI capabilities, data/telemetry

programs, analytics or tool rollouts) with clear milestones, owners, and success metrics.

• Build and maintain program roadmaps, dependency maps, and risk registers; proactively identify

and resolve blockers across teams.

• Drive operating rhythms (standups, reviews, steering forums) with AI Research, AI Engineering,

Robotics Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, and AI Product Management.

• Roll up your sleeves to push work through organizational and process complexity—coordinating

with IT, Purchasing, Vendors, Finance, HR, and other partners to keep programs moving.

• Comfortably manage multiple initiatives at once, switching contexts between short-turnaround

deliverables and long-horizon programs without dropping details

Strategy, storytelling, and decision support

• Partner with leadership to define and refine Robotics AI strategy, including problem selection,

sequencing of bets, and success metrics.

• Structure clear narratives and storyboards that connect technical work to GM-level business

outcomes and manufacturing KPIs.

• Prepare executive-ready presentations and decision docs (SVP and above), highlighting what

has changed, what is at risk, and what decisions are needed.

• Translate complex technical options into simple, structured trade-off frameworks for senior

decision-makers.

Data, analytics, and tooling

• Go deep on data: define questions, shape logging/telemetry requirements, pull and analyze data

using SQL, Python, or R, and translate findings into actionable insights.

• Build and maintain dashboards (e.g., Looker, Power BI) that track program KPIs, model and

system performance, factory deployment health, and operational metrics.

• Partner with Data Engineering and platform teams to leverage Databricks and other

infrastructure for analytics and reporting.

• Design and orchestrate GenAI-powered workflows and agents to automate repetitive analysis,

reporting, and operational tasks where appropriate.

• Continuously learn and adopt new AI, data, dashboarding, and tracking tools, and help the

broader team do the same

AI, robotics, and technical collaboration

• Act as a fluent technical partner to AI researchers, robotics engineers, and data engineers—you

don’t need to write production code or models, but you do need to understand what makes them

hard.

• Help ensure that data collection, labeling, evaluation, and deployment workstreams are

aligned with program goals and success metrics.

• Collaborate closely with AI product managers to connect user needs, technical capabilities,

and deployment constraints, especially in manufacturing settings.

• Engage with external partners and vendors in AI, robotics, and data tooling where both technical

depth and program context are required.

Ways of working and culture

• Champion a learning-oriented culture: rapidly explore new tools (GenAI, agents, analytics,

low-code platforms), techniques, and methodologies, and help the team adopt what works.

• Model “get your hands dirty” execution—whether that’s pulling data, building a quick

dashboard, prototyping an AI agent, or refining a deck the night before an exec review.

• Help continuously improve our program management, measurement, and communication

practices across the Robotics AI org.

• Practice proactive, “over-communication” with leaders and stakeholders—keeping partners up to

speed on risks, decisions, and progress, and responding quickly to questions or asks

• Thrive in a dynamic environment where priorities can shift, and enjoy moving between strategic

problem framing, detailed data work, and day-to-day execution

What you bring

Required qualifications

• Bachelor’s or higher degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical

Engineering, or a closely related technical field.

• 4+ years of experience in one or more of:

o Management consulting or corporate strategy

o Product management or technical program management

o Data science or data analytics

• Meaningful experience in AI, ML, or robotics (e.g., robotics AI, applied ML, computer vision,

intelligent automation, or similar), ideally at the intersection of AI and robotics.

• Demonstrated ability to lead large, complex cross-functional programs with high ambiguity and

multiple parallel workstreams.

• Strong strategic thinking and storytelling skills: can frame problems, structure options, and

communicate clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.

• Comfort operating as a hands-on analyst and builder, including:

o Writing SQL and using Python or R for analysis

o Building dashboards in tools like Looker or Power BI

o Working in Databricks and similar data platforms

• Demonstrated fluency with GenAI tools (e.g., prompt engineering, using copilots/assistants in

daily workflows) and a track record of designing or orchestrating AI-assisted workflows or

agents.

• Experience with modern collaboration and delivery tooling such as Jira and low/no-code

application platforms (e.g., Power Apps, AppSheet).

• Ability to modulate communication style: comfortable diving into technical details with AI

researchers and roboticists, and equally comfortable presenting synthesized insights to senior,

non-technical executives.

• Proven cross-functional collaboration and influence skills; known as a team player who

creates clarity and momentum rather than just tracking tasks.

• Demonstrated experience working directly with technical teams (AI researchers, AI engineers,

roboticists, data engineers), understanding their work well enough to track progress, surface

risks, and offer hands-on support

Strongly preferred

• Prior work in robotics, robotics AI, or physical AI systems, especially in manufacturing,

industrial, or logistics environments.

• Experience operating at the intersection of research and production, helping teams balance

exploration with delivery.

• Background in data-driven decision-making, experimentation, and KPI design in complex

technical domains.

• Experience defining and instrumenting metrics for AI or robotics systems (e.g., reliability,

coverage, cycle time, throughput, data quality).

• Comfort with storyboarding and narrative design—you naturally think in terms of “what’s the

story?” and how to land it in a deck or memo.

• Track record of rapidly learning new technical domains and tools and helping teams adopt

them effectively.

• Experience driving programs through enterprise processes (e.g., security reviews, procurement,

vendor onboarding) and removing organizational blockers to keep technical teams moving.

Who you are

• Strategic and big-picture thinker who can also go deep into the data and technical details when

needed, and who enjoys switching between high-level framing and hands-on execution.

• Storyteller and storyboarder who can craft clear narratives from complex technical work,

elevating the message for SVP-level audiences while making it appropriately technical for AI

researchers and engineers.

• Cross-functional collaborator who builds trust with engineers, researchers, product leaders,

and manufacturing partners, and is known as an operator/hustler who gets things done across

organizational boundaries.

• Curious, hungry learner of new tools, techniques, and subject areas; you proactively experiment

with new AI and analytics capabilities, and quickly incorporate them into how you and the team

work.

• Hands-on and detail-oriented, willing to get into the weeds on data, tools, and process to make

programs successful, from small, fast-turnaround analyses to multi-quarter initiatives.

• Technically fluent, able to understand AI and robotics concepts well enough to ask the right

questions and bridge between disciplines, and comfortable interfacing directly with AI

researchers, AI engineers, and roboticists on a daily basis.

• A proactive, “over-communicating” operator who keeps stakeholders informed, surfaces risks

early, and follows through reliably - especially when juggling multiple priorities at once

Location & team




• You will sit within GM’s AI Product Management and Strategy organization, working directly with

the Robotics AI team and partnering closely with AI Research, AI Engineering, Robotics

Engineering, Data Engineering, and Manufacturing Engineering.

• This is a high-visibility role with regular exposure to senior leadership and key external

technology partners

title: Senior Robotics Software Engineer
description:
As a Robotics Software Engineer on the Isaac Applications Team, you will bring together the software and hardware that enable Physical AI robots to operate in the real world. You will build working robotic systems and end-to-end workflows for engineers and AI agents. These workflows connect data, simulation, and real-world deployment to continuously expand and improve robot capabilities.

  


We’re looking for strong software engineering skills, broad robotics knowledge, and enthusiasm for working hands-on with physical robots when taking ideas into practice. You enjoy understanding how components interact, solving problems across their boundaries, and seeing them come together to deliver new robot capabilities.

  


## What you will be doing:

  * Lead the forefront of Physical AI progress in both simulated and real humanoid robots by building the humanoid reference platform that features NVIDIA's robotics technologies.
  * Build end-to-end workflows to develop, evaluate, and deploy increasingly autonomous and interactive robot capabilities.
  * Extend our platform to new robot embodiments and demonstrate its adaptability through hands-on integration and validation. Address real-world compute, latency, and bandwidth constraints on physical hardware.
  * Collaborate across teams in Shanghai, America, and Europe to connect capabilities and deliver reliable robotic systems.

  


## What we need to see:

  * Master’s degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
  * 8+ years of relevant industry experience working on robotics software.
  * Hands-on experience integrating, deploying, and testing software on physical robots, and confidence working directly with hardware when needed.
  * Experience deploying and evaluating learned policies to control physical robots.
  * Broad working knowledge of robotics software, hardware, AI, and agentic systems. We value an understanding of how these components interact within a complete system.
  * Strong problem-solving skills, including tracing issues across software and hardware boundaries. Ability to work independently through ambiguous technical challenges.
  * Interest in designing robotics interfaces for agent-driven operation, with the ability to learn and evaluate new approaches.

  


## Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd:

  * Experience integrating humanoid robots or mobile manipulators, from initial bring-up through reliable demonstrations of robot capabilities.
  * Experience diagnosing and resolving system-level challenges across robotics software and hardware.
  * Experience building end-to-end robotics workflows where AI agents perform substantial portions of the work and guide engineers through data collection, training, evaluation, and deployment.



Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and the pay of employees in similar positions. The base salary range is 184,000 USD - 287,500 USD for Level 4, and 224,000 USD - 356,500 USD for Level 5.

You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.

Applications for this job will be accepted at least until October 20, 2026.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

NVIDIA is committed to fostering an inclusive work environment and proud to be an equal opportunity employer. As we highly value diversity in our current and future employees, we do not discriminate (including in our hiring and promotion practices) on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status or any other characteristic protected by law.

At Lucid, we are creating exceptional mobility experiences through innovation to drive the world forward. The PositionSenior Principal Robotics Engineer - CVRM

 

ITOT supports Pharma Technical Manufacturing (PTM), PTM is responsible for managing all aspects of end-to-end drug substance and drug product manufacturing and supply. From the raw material to the final medicine, we contribute to delivering Roche’s ground-breaking therapies to more than 120 million patients around the world. We make our medicines at nine sites around the world and coordinate all aspects of production of Roche medicines in all disease areas and dosage forms. To ensure readiness for a step-change in the standard of care that Roche delivers in the area of Cardiovascular, Renal and Metabolism (CVRM), PTM will construct a new manufacturing site in the U.S. in Holly Spring, North Carolina. ITOT will own and operate Manufacturing Technology stack at the site working with Global IT. The new site will focus on large volume low-cost Drug Product manufacturing (Component Prep & Compounding, Liquid PFS Filling, Automated Inspection, Autoinjector Assembly, Packaging/Finished Products).

 

The Opportunity

The Senior Principal Robotics Engineer will build, gain approval for, and fully implement the comprehensive robotics program for the Holly Springs Greenfield project. The role is essential for transforming the site's manual operations into a "Smart Factory" model, targeting a state-of-the-art Highly Automated Warehouse and the integration of Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) throughout the facility.

 

Initially, you will perform a mix of remote and onsite work (first at the General Planner’s office, later at construction site/plant). You will transition to local full-time on-site work once the site buildings are built and equipment delivered. Eventually, you will transition into the site-based robotics systems owner and provide site operations support on robotics. Travel of up to 30% of the time is expected during the project phase.

 

What You Will Do

Program Development & Implementation: Create full context about the Holly Springs Robotics strategy to hone, get approval, and implement the comprehensive Holly Springs robotics program.System Ownership & Support: Eventually become the dedicated site-based robotics systems owner and provide ongoing, 24/7 site operations support on robotics once the facility goes live.Team Leadership: Possibly manage a team of robotics engineers in the future, scaling the team based on business needs and commercial filling requirements.Robotics PIT Leadership: Serve on the Robotics Project Implementation Team (PIT) to focus on robotics and technical enablement, implementation of industry standards, and ensuring seamless compatibility, connectivity, and data integrity.Smart Factory Integration: Lead the transition of manual operations into a "Smart Factory" model, integrating Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs), AGVs (e.g., MiR, Geek+), and ASRS systems across end-to-end flows (kitting, filling, packaging, waste handling).Strategy & Roadmap Creation: Formulate a capability roadmap and investment case to articulate the ROI of robotic interventions based on labor savings, ergonomic risks, and increased facility uptime.System Qualification: Support end-to-end system qualification, including test creation, execution, and approval, working alongside IT/OT to integrate robotics into the digital twin and enterprise architecture.Safety & Compliance: Ensure the integration of environmental health, safety, and security into the business processes, and adhere to site SOPs and work instructions for daily and project deliverables.

description:
I. About the Role

VinDynamics is developing next-generation humanoid robots capable of performing complex tasks in home and office environments.

We are seeking talented AI Robot Engineers specializing in Whole-Body Manipulation to join our team to develop and deploy AI models that enable humanoid robots to coordinate locomotion, balance, and manipulation to perform real-world tasks.




II. Key Responsibilities

Whole-Body Manipulation: Develop learning-based policies that coordinate the hands, arms, and whole body for reaching, grasping, lifting, carrying, and other contact-rich manipulation tasks.Robot Learning: Apply reinforcement learning (RL), imitation learning (IL), vision-language-action (VLA) models, World Action Models (WAM), and motion tracking to develop robust humanoid manipulation and loco-manipulation skills.Simulation & Training: Build scalable training pipelines using Isaac Lab, Isaac Sim, MuJoCo, or similar simulators, including reward design, curriculum learning, and domain randomization.Human Motion Learning: Leverage human motion-capture data, teleoperation, demonstrations, and egocentric data for motion retargeting, imitation learning, and policy improvement.Sim-to-Real Deployment: Transfer trained policies to physical humanoid robots, optimize real-time inference, and improve robustness and task success rates in real-world environments.System Integration: Integrate AI models with whole-body controllers, motion planners, perception systems, and vision-language-action (VLA) models.


III. Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications 

Master’s or Ph.D. degree in Robotics, Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Control Engineering, or related fields.2+ years of experience applying multimodal data to train AI models for robotic manipulation.Strong understanding of data types and data requirements to train AI models for whole-body manipulation.Strong understanding of reinforcement learning, imitation learning, VLA models, diffusion-based methods, World Action Model (WAM),Solid understanding of robot kinematics and dynamics, and feedback control.Strong programming skills in Python, C++, and PyTorch.Hands-on experience with robotic simulation platforms such as Isaac Lab, Isaac Sim, or MuJoCo.Experience developing and training policies for robot manipulation, locomotion, or whole-body control.Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to design, evaluate, and debug robotic learning systems.Preferred Qualifications 

Experience deploying learning-based policies on physical humanoid, quadruped, or robotic manipulation platforms.Familiarity with PPO, actor-critic methods, imitation learning, motion tracking, and sim-to-real transfer.Experience with human motion retargeting, teleoperation data collection, and large-scale robot learning pipelines.Experience deploying AI models on real robots, including optimization for real-time inference.Experience with bimanual manipulation, dexterous hands, and contact-rich manipulation tasks.Familiarity with ROS 2, VLA models, diffusion policies, or robotics foundation models.Publications or open-source contributions in robotics, robot learning, or embodied AI are a plus.


IV. What You Will Build

Whole-Body Reaching: Humanoid robots that bend, squat, step, and reach to manipulate objects.Loco-Manipulation: Robots that walk while grasping, lifting, and carrying objects.Bimanual Manipulation: Coordinated two-arm manipulation with balance-aware control.Real-World Autonomy: Robust whole-body skills integrated with perception and high-level task planning.

    **_What Data Science contributes to Cardinal Health_**
      
    The Data and Analytics Function oversees the analytics life-cycle in order to identify, analyze and present relevant insights that drive business decisions and anticipate opportunities to achieve a competitive advantage. This function manages analytic data platforms, the access, design and implementation of reporting/business intelligence solutions, and the application of advanced quantitative modeling. Data Science applies base, scientific methodologies from various disciplines, techniques and tools that extracts knowledge and insight from data to solve complex business problems on large data sets, integrating multiple systems.
      
    **_Department/Team Overview_**
      
    We are looking for a Data Scientist, Operations Research Analyst to join our Decision Science Solutions (DS2) team. Our mission is to improve our pharmaceutical supply chain’s performance to better service our pharmacy customers, so that they can focus on their patients. The DS2 team consists of Supply Chain Data Scientists, Operations Research Analysts, Data Analysts, and Data Engineers. We work cross-functionally to solve problems leveraging a variety of skillsets and perspectives to achieve the best outcomes. We perform analyses, recommend solutions, and build products to enable better decision making in the following areas:
      
    + Distribution center network design and capacity planning
      
    + Facility layout and design; warehouse capacity and utilization
      
    + Warehouse process improvement
      
    + Labor management and automation
      
    + Inventory management: stocking strategies and replenishment policies
      
    + Transportation planning: first mile, middle mile, and final mile
      
    + Sales and operations planning (resource management in response to demand changes)
      
    **_Responsibilities_**
      
    As a Data Scientist in Supply Chain Operations, you will apply your knowledge of business processes, systems, data, and analytical tools to explore and identify root causes of problems. You will forecast future demand, build optimization and simulation models, and communicate actionable insights. You will work with cross-functional project teams to ideate, develop, and recommend solutions. Specific responsibilities are to:
      
    + Listen to clients and ask questions to clearly define business problems.
      
    + Perform exploratory analysis to determine root causes of problems and confirm/disprove hypotheses.
      
    + Develop predictive models to forecast future volumes that will drive capacity/resource needs.
      
    + Develop customer and product segmentation models and design our supply chain to support differentiated services.
      
    + Build optimization and simulation models to recommend capacity investments, resource plans, policy changes, and process changes to improve supply chain performance.
      
    + Develop prescriptive models using 3rd party optimization/simulation software and custom-build models.
      
    + Recommend solutions. Summarize the financial and operational impact of the recommendation and pros/cons of alternatives considered.
      
    + Work with Data Engineers to create data models for analyses.
      
    **_Qualifications_**
      
    + 2-4 years of experience, preferred
      
    + Bachelor's degree in a quantitative field, or equivalent work experience, preferred
      
    + MS/MBA with focus in Data Science, Operations Research, Industrial Engineering, or Statistics preferred
      
    + Demonstrated ability to apply Data Science and Operations Research techniques to logistics and supply chain management problems preferred
      
    + Experience with Structured Query Language (SQL) and working with databases preferred
      
    + Experience with data analysis tools such as R, Python, SQL, Alteryx, Tableau, and SAS preferred
      
    + Experience with Strategic Network Design, Simulation (e.g., AnyLogic), or Mathematical Programming (e.g., CPLEX) software preferred
      
    + Ability to work as part of a team as the key analytical resource
      
    + Excellent communication skills with an ability to explain quantitative analysis in simple business terms
      
    + Intellectual curiosity, humility, genuine respect and desire to help others
      
    + Bias for action and passion for driving change
      
    + Ability to travel up to 5%
      
    **_What is expected of you and others at this level_**
      
    + Applies comprehensive knowledge and a thorough understanding of concepts, principles, and technical capabilities to perform varied tasks and projects
      
    + May contribute to the development of policies and procedures
      
    + Works on complex projects of large scope
      
    + Develops technical solutions to a wide range of difficult problems
      
    + Solutions are innovative and consistent with organization objectives
      
    + Completes work; independently receives general guidance on new projects
      
    + Work reviewed for purpose of meeting objectives
      
    + May act as a mentor to less experienced colleagues

Peraton is currently hiring an Operations Research Analyst (with Working Knowledge of AI Tools for Regression Testing) – Joint Deployment and Distribution Enterprise (JDDE) for the Joint Distribution Process Analysis Center (JDPAC) at USTRANSCOM.

Peraton is seeking an Operations Research Analyst to join our mission to provide analytical support to improve the nation's ability to move and sustain forces globally, leveraging platforms such as Maven Smart System and Palantir Foundry.


In this position, you will:



Provide support for Research, Development, Testing & Evaluation (RDT&E) for Modeling, Simulation & Optimization (MS&O) applications and prototypes produced in support of or being adapted for JDDE movement processes.

Analyze operational activities to obtain a quantitative, rational basis for decision making through the application of logic, scientific, and economic disciplines and techniques.
Devise modeling and measuring techniques; utilize mathematics, statistical methods, engineering methods, operational mathematics techniques (linear programming, game theory, probability theory, symbolic language, etc.), and other principles and laws of scientific and economic disciplines.
Use Maven Smart System and Palantir Foundry for scripting and automating regression tests to ensure the reliability of legacy code as new code is deployed.

Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in Operations Research, Industrial Engineering, Science, Economics, Mathematics, Statistics, Business, Computer Science, or similar fields and a minimum of 2 years of experience.

Experience using Maven Smart System and/or Palantir Foundry for data analysis or testing.
Working knowledge of AI tools and scripting languages (such as Python or R) for regression testing and automation.

Demonstrated analytical, quantitative reasoning, mathematical, and problem-solving skills.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Experience with MS Excel.
Familiarity with the Joint Deployment and Distribution Enterprise either as a former operator, planner, or enabling support function.

Active DoD Secret clearance.
Master’s degree.

Advanced familiarity with JDDE.
Experience with Python programming for scripting and testing.
Experience with MS Office including MS Teams.
Experience with R programming language.
Experience writing and automating regression tests using AI tools within Maven Smart System and Palantir Foundry.

At Frontier, our mission is to Make Every Flight Count. That mission guides how we support our customers, our people and the operation every day.

Frontier offers benefits, programs and travel privileges designed to support eligible employees at work and beyond. Availability may vary by role, employment status, eligibility, location, schedule, applicable policies and current plan details.

About Frontier Airlines

Frontier Airlines is a Denver-based airline serving destinations across the United States and select international markets. Our people support every part of the travel journey, from airport operations and flight crews to aircraft maintenance, customer support, corporate teams and more.

We’re focused on delivering meaningful value by making travel more accessible, practical and easy to personalize for our customers. Across the airline, our teams help support a safe, reliable and efficient operation while continuing to strengthen the experience for the people who choose Frontier.

What Will You Be Doing?

As the Operations Research Senior Analyst, you will play a pivotal role in transforming the data and analytics environment at Frontier Airlines. This role will serve as a highly analytical and versatile contributor within the Operations Analytics team, supporting enterprise operational decision making through data engineering, advanced analytics, operational research, reporting automation, and strategic analysis.

The ideal candidate will function as a “Swiss Army knife” across operations analytics, partnering with operational departments to identify performance opportunities, develop scalable data solutions, generate actionable insights, and present findings to leadership up to and including executive leadership.

Essential Functions

• Analyze large operational datasets to identify trends, performance gaps, operational risks, and improvement opportunities

• Apply operations research, statistical, forecasting, simulation, and analytical techniques to solve complex airline operational problems

• Design, develop, test, and refine predictive, optimization, simulation, and statistical models using operations research and data science methodologies

• Support operational initiatives including block time development, turn time analysis, schedule reliability, delay analysis, and operational efficiency studies

• Develop, maintain, and enhance operational datasets, data pipelines, and reporting solutions supporting the airline’s operational single source of truth

• Develop and automate dashboards, scorecards, and reporting tools using Power BI and related technologies

• Translate complex technical and analytical findings into clear, actionable recommendations for operational and executive leadership

• Partner cross-functionally with operational departments including Tech Ops, Flight Operations, Inflight, Ground Operations, and System Operations

• Prepare executive ready presentations, reports, and analyses for leadership meetings and operational reviews

• Maintain data governance standards, metric definitions, and documentation to ensure consistency and accuracy across operational reporting

• Support ad hoc analyses, special projects, and continuous improvement initiatives across the operation

Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Operations Research, Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Engineering, Computer Science, related quantitative field, or equivalent experience required

• Master’s degree in same fields or equivalent experience preferred

• 4+ years of experience in analytics, operations research, business intelligence, data science, data engineering, or related analytical roles

• Professional experience using SQL and Python to analyze and manipulate large datasets

• Experience developing dashboards and visualizations using Power BI, Tableau, or similar business intelligence platforms

• Experience in the airline industry, operational analytics, Databricks, or advanced quantitative modeling preferred

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

• Strong proficiency in SQL for querying, transforming, and optimizing large operational datasets

• Strong proficiency in Python for analytics, automation, and data engineering applications

• Experience working within Databricks or similar cloud-based analytics environments

• Experience developing dashboards and interactive visualizations using Power BI or similar tools

• Familiarity with AI supported coding and analytical tools, such as Claude, ChatGPT, or similar technologies

• Ability to analyze complex operational data and identify actionable business insights and recommendations

• Understanding of statistical analysis, forecasting, optimization, simulation, or machine learning concepts

• Familiarity with data modeling, ETL/ELT processes, data governance, and enterprise analytics architecture

• Strong critical thinking and root cause analysis capabilities

• Ability to communicate complex analytical findings to both technical and non-technical audiences

• Strong written, verbal, presentation, and executive communication skills

• Ability to build executive ready PowerPoint presentations and operational summaries

• Ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively in a fast-paced operational environment

• Strong collaboration and stakeholder management skills across operational departments

• High attention to detail, intellectual curiosity, and commitment to data accuracy and integrity

Typical office environment, adequately heated and cooled

Generally, not required.

title: Operations Research Systems Analyst
description:
Overview
The Operations Research Systems Analyst (ORSA) applies advanced quantitative methods, mathematical modeling, and systems analysis to optimize complex intelligence and operational processes across the Joint Intelligence Operations Center (JIOC). This position supports data-driven decision-making by developing rigorous analytical solutions to multifaceted mission challenges, providing actionable insights to senior leaders, and enhancing the efficiency and effectiveness of intelligence operations.


The ORSA works at the intersection of analytics, operations, and strategy—translating complex datasets and system behaviors into clear, evidence-based recommendations that shape operational planning and enterprise-level decision cycles.


Responsibilities

Develop and apply mathematical models, optimization techniques, and algorithmic solutions to improve intelligence operations and resource utilization.
Conduct systematic analyses of operational workflows to identify inefficiencies, quantify impacts, and recommend improvements.
Perform statistical analysis and experimental design to evaluate system performance and test operational hypotheses.
Build and run discrete event simulations to model complex operational scenarios and assess potential courses of action.
Apply decision analysis and risk assessment methodologies to support planning in uncertain and dynamic environments.
Develop, measure, and assess operational metrics, including Measures of Performance (MOPs), Measures of Effectiveness (MOEs), and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs).
Design data collection strategies to ensure accurate and comprehensive evaluation of operational systems.
Evaluate system performance using quantitative techniques and provide recommendations for optimization.
Prepare analytical reports, dashboards, and visualizations explaining findings to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Brief complex analysis and model results to senior leadership to support data-driven decision-making.
Support operational planning teams with quantitative insights and structured analytical methodologies.
Identify opportunities to improve processes, automate tasks, and enhance mission performance.
Develop custom analytical tools, models, and approaches tailored to specific intelligence or operational requirements.
Participate in JIOC intelligence planning conferences, exercises, J2 working groups, capability development sessions, national-level coordination boards, and technical exchange meetings.

Qualifications

Education



Master’s degree or Ph.D. in Operations Research, Systems Engineering, Mathematics, Statistics, or a related quantitative discipline.
Required Skills



Advanced expertise in multiple OR methodologies (optimization, stochastic modeling, simulation, systems analysis).
Deep understanding of complex systems modeling and quantitative problem-solving.
Proven success applying OR techniques to real-world operational challenges.
Experience with R, Python, MATLAB, or equivalent analytical software.
Experience designing and implementing enterprise-level metrics and performance frameworks.
Advanced knowledge of experimental design, statistical inference, and simulation development.
Ability to create complex simulation models tailored to operational environments.
Strategic thinking that aligns analytical findings with mission priorities and decision-maker requirements.
Experience



Minimum 8+ years of OR, systems analysis, or related analytical experience, with demonstrated impact on operational effectiveness and mission outcomes.

description:
At MITRE, your passion fuels work that impacts our nation and improves lives. This is where your skills strengthen national security, cybersecurity, health, transportation, and citizen services. We’re a nonprofit engineering, applied research, and advanced technology organization working in the public interest.  With objectivity and integrity at our core, we lead federally funded research and development centers for U.S. government agencies – collaborating with industry and academia to deliver integrated, high-impact solutions that advance our nation’s health, security, and prosperity.  Our people tackle the toughest technical challenges, supported by competitive benefits, meaningful career development, and a culture of innovation, collaboration, and technical excellence. Choose MITRE for a career with purpose — and help shape the future.



Department Summary:

 

Shape the Future of National Security—Join MITRE and Tackle the Toughest Challenges with Innovation and Impact!


Are you an experienced professional passionate about solving complex challenges to safeguard our nation? At MITRE, you’ll collaborate with top minds in engineering, science, and technology, leveraging cutting-edge research and experimentation to address the nation’s most pressing challenges.

 

MITRE is a nonprofit systems engineering, applied research, and advanced technology organization that operates federally funded R&D centers to deliver deep technical and systems integration, rapid prototype development, and mission-driven innovation in the public interest. Headquarters are in McLean, Virginia and Bedford, Massachusetts are supported by over 60 sites across the U.S. and globe to bring solutions to the field.

 

MITRE Technology and Engineering Modeling and Analysis (M&A) Division brings together researchers, autonomy engineers, mission specialists, and systems experts to translate advanced research into operationally relevant solutions. M&A is seeking modeling and simulation engineers and operations research analysts to support the operations analysis and complex systems modeling work across MITRE’s national security and public sector missions.   

 

 

Roles & Responsibilities:


We are seeking an experienced, highly motivated Modeling & Simulation / Operations Research Analyst to support critical national security missions. In this role, you will partner with operational stakeholders to develop and apply advanced modeling, simulation, and analytical tools—integrating mathematics, physics, engineering, and programming—to generate actionable insights for mission and sponsor needs.

 

You will tackle complex, real-world problems at the intersection of technology and national security while expanding your skills through hands-on work. We value curiosity, innovation, and a passion for learning, and we’re looking for candidates who thrive in collaborative, diverse teams and are committed to delivering solutions that make a real impact.

 

Responsibilities include:


Contribute to the development and application of modeling and simulation tools by providing technical expertise and support.Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to refine methodologies and address technical challenges.Shape project strategies by identifying and recommending innovative techniques and tools to improve modeling, simulation, and analysis capabilities.Communicate findings and recommendations to stakeholders to ensure alignment with mission goals.Support collaboration across teams to enhance the effectiveness and scalability of modeling, simulation, and analysis initiatives.

title: Lead Applied Operations Research Analyst
description:
At MITRE, your passion fuels work that impacts our nation and improves lives. This is where your skills strengthen national security, cybersecurity, health, transportation, and citizen services. We’re a nonprofit engineering, applied research, and advanced technology organization working in the public interest. With objectivity and integrity at our core, we lead federally funded research and development centers for U.S. government agencies – collaborating with industry and academia to deliver integrated, high-impact solutions that advance our nation’s health, security, and prosperity. Our people tackle the toughest technical challenges, supported by competitive benefits, meaningful career development, and a culture of innovation, collaboration, and technical excellence. Choose MITRE for a career with purpose — and help shape the future. 
 


  Department Summary:


 


 

   This is an opportunity for a motivated Operations Research Analyst to join MITRE’s Operations Analysis department. We are a large group of over 60 operations research professionals, including over 20 PhDs, who provide thought leadership on a variety of strategic and technical issues, perform analysis that enable our sponsors to make more effective decisions, lead internal research and development activities to bring new technical capabilities into the public sector, and serve as trusted third-party advisors to government sponsors on a variety of technical topics.


 


 

   In short, we apply our problem-solving skills to complex interdisciplinary problems that occur within or at the intersection of organizations, operations, and technology. We support sponsor projects across the defense and public sectors including homeland defense, military logistics, radio-spectrum frequency management, health care delivery, cybersecurity analytics, fraud detection, satellite planning, homeland security and civilian aviation. We apply advanced analytic techniques such as longitudinal analysis, large-scale integer programming, metaheuristics, agent-based modeling, reinforcement learning, predictive modeling, mathematical modeling, time series & forecasting, machine learning, optimization, statistics, probability modeling, regression analyses, Bayesian analysis, and different types of simulation to solve the nation’s toughest problems. And our research pushes the boundaries on topics such as complex scheduling, medical image analysis, identifying changes in data streams and incorporating the latest AI advancements into our processes for efficiency and rigor.


 


 

   If you are passionate about project-based analytical work in the public interest, you have found the right place.


 


 

    Roles & Responsibilities:


 

 
  Apply advanced analytical and mathematical modeling techniques to inform difficult policy and acquisition decisions, to maximize operational effectiveness and efficiency, and achieve highest quality engineering solutions
  Frame problems, collect and manipulate data, develop & code customized algorithms, identify risks, and incorporate domain-specific context, as necessary & applicable, to supplement and enhance insight gained solely from mathematical analyses
  Present results in an intuitive, actionable manner that can be understood by all sponsor audiences, regardless of technical expertise, including creative data visualization artifacts
  Work independently and collaborate with a team of technical staff and domain experts
  Work successfully both in a remote environment and with in-person presence
 
 


 

    Basic Qualifications:


 

 


 
  Typically requires a minimum of 8 years of related experience with a Bachelor’s degree in Operations Research, Industrial Engineering, Data Science/Analytics, Applied Mathematics/Statistics, or equivalent knowledge and skills in a related field or 6 years and a Master’s degree; or a PhD with 3 years of experience or equivalent combination of related education and work experience.
  Be passionate about applying operations research, statistics, and data analytics to real world problems
  Be willing to adapt and learn
  Demonstrated ability to use at least one optimization package (e.g., Gurobi, CPLEX, PuLP, AMPL)
  Demonstrated ability to use at least one modern programming language (e.g., Python, R, Java)
  Demonstrated ability to use at least one simulation platform (e.g., Stella, Simio, Arena, AnyLogic, SimPy, RSimmer)
   Must have an active Secret U.S Government issued Security Clearance and must be eligible to obtain and maintain a Top Secret U.S Government issued Security Clearance. Per the U.S. Government’s eligibility requirements, you must be a U.S Citizen to be considered for a security clearance.
  This position requires 4 days a week on site
 
 


 

    Preferred Qualifications:


 

 
  Master’s or Ph.D. degree in Operations Research, Industrial Engineering, Data Science/Analytics, Applied Mathematics/Statistics, or equivalent knowledge and skills in a related field
  Preference given to qualified candidates with active clearance (e.g. TS/SCI)
  Experience working with/for agencies and/or departments of the US Government (e.g., FAA, DoD, DoE, DHS, Treasury, IRS)
  Demonstrated ability to develop and incorporate a variety of AI/ML models, techniques, and principles into analytical work to efficiently achieve rigorous outcomes
  Familiarity and/or experience with Electromagnetic Spectrum (EMS) organizations, concepts, modeling, testing, and assessment, to include the Joint Electromagnetic Spectrum Operations Center (JEC), Joint Electromagnetic Warfare Center (JEWC), Electromagnetic Spectrum Operations (EMSO), Electromagnetic Battle Management—Joint (EMBM-J), Spectrum Consumption Modeling (SCM), and Electronic Warfare (EW)
  Familiarity and/or experience with the Mission Engineering paradigm of decomposing a key operational problem, establishing a system-of-systems model of components, technology, policies, procedures, and techniques, and ultimately simulating the process on a technical platform

 Top Secret
