description:
About this Role👋 Hi, I’m Kevin. I manage the Data team and our analytics products at Ashby. I’m hiring our first Data Analytics Manager at an important point in Ashby’s growth, and I hope you have the patience to read a job posting that may be a little unconventional.

You will manage Ashby’s three Data Analysts: two core analysts and one analyst focused on Revenue Operations. Our Data Engineer will initially continue to report directly to me, so this role is deliberately more focused on the analytical side of the team while remaining a close partner in the broader data ecosystem.

The primary result of your successful management will be a team of analysts with excellent judgment, strong technical methods, clear communication, and a deep sense of ownership. I am looking for someone who can help that team do better work, choose better work, and grow into the next stage of Ashby alongside the company.

Rather than begin with a long list of tools or years of experience, I want to share four questions that sit at the center of this role. If you apply, your answer should be “yes” to each. Should we get a chance to talk, what I will really want to understand is the nuance: your unique how, why, and what behind your answers.

Can you identify and hire talented people?

We will continue to grow the analyst team, and you will play a meaningful role in finding and assessing future teammates. Great analysts combine technical judgment, curiosity, communication, business context, and a willingness to own work end to end. Can you recognize that combination in others?

Can you develop and amplify the data practices that let a small team do excellent work?

Ashby’s Data team is lean, and our practices will need to evolve as the company becomes more complex. I see this role as an opportunity to improve the ways we prioritize work, review it, share knowledge, maintain quality, and collaborate.

Can you lead the team through the transition from broad shared context to meaningful specialization?

Today, each analyst can know a great deal about the company and data stack. That will become more challenging as Ashby grows across products, regions, systems, and business functions. We will need to develop stronger domain context and clearer ways of working without turning the team into a set of narrow, disconnected specialists.

Can you help the Data team navigate the rapidly evolving implications of AI?

AI will affect how our analysts work, how the company self-serves analytical questions, and how other teams use internal business data. Much of that work depends on trusted, well-modeled, appropriately accessible warehouse-derived data. You will help the Data team explore and evaluate the relevant tools, workflows, and partnerships—bringing ambition, practicality, and a high bar for accuracy.

These questions add up to a simple reality: Ashby is growing quickly, and the surrounding data needs are becoming more complex. We are becoming a multi-product, global company with more business systems and larger team dynamics. This is a great opportunity at a great company, but it will be hard and consequential work. I am looking for a manager who is excited to help shape the Data function and build an excellent team for its current and future members.


Your responsibilities as a Data Analytics ManagerTo understand the role, it helps to understand how our team works today.

Data Analysts at Ashby are full-stack members of the Data team. We do not have a traditional split where Analytics Engineers build models and Data Analysts perform analysis only on prepared datasets. Our analysts work across raw and modeled data, contribute to dbt models and metric definitions, conduct deep analysis, build dashboards and other internal data products, and collaborate directly with partners throughout the company.

As a rough sketch, the team receives work through a standardized request process. Anyone can make a request; we triage it, assess the actual need, and decide whether it can be addressed quickly or should become a more deliberate project with a kickoff and plan. We do not currently organize ourselves around universal SLAs, sprints, or points. Instead, we aim to be good partners: communicate clearly, assess capacity honestly, prioritize thoughtfully, and make deliberate choices about what not to do. You will have a lot of leverage in aiding this process well.

Ashby’s Operating Principles place principled thinking ahead of reflexively leaning on prior experience or convention. In practice, that means work at Ashby does not always start with “let’s get all the data and metrics.” Data is one useful tool for resolving uncertainty; it is not automatically the first or only tool. That said, as the company matures and more teams optimize their work, demand for data will likely continue to grow. You will help us meet that demand with good judgment.


Why You Should or Shouldn’t ApplyAt Ashby’s current size, this is a player-coach role. You should expect to get hands-on with analytical work as you learn the business and the team, and to remain close enough to the work to guide its quality well.

You could be a strong fit if you:

Have exceptional analytical judgment. You can calibrate the depth and rigor of an analysis to the decision at hand: knowing when precision matters, when uncertainty is material, and when additional work would not change the outcome.

Can produce and evaluate transparent, rigorous analysis. You bring readers along through the problem context, data considered, assumptions, meaningful cleaning or reduction steps, caveats, statistical pitfalls, and practical conclusion.

Are a strong visual and written communicator. You care about clear tables and charts, meaningful labels and definitions, coherent narratives, and making complex work understandable without overstating certainty.

Have deep hands-on SQL experience, plus working fluency with dbt-style data modeling, cloud data warehouses, and BI tools. You do not need to have owned a warehouse as a Data Engineer, but you should be comfortable working across the analytical data stack.

Have led, managed, or functionally acted as a manager for data practitioners in a high-growth company. Formal people-management experience is valuable, but not required if you have demonstrated equivalent judgment, coaching, hiring, and team-leadership abilities.

Bring a product-manager-like instinct for finding the core need behind a request, understanding users and business context, and turning ambiguous questions into useful work.

Are pragmatic and intellectually flexible. You see data as one important input to good judgment alongside qualitative research, collaboration, user understanding, and clear thinking.

Are intimately familiar with the B2B SaaS industry, workflows and organizational structures.

Have an eye and instinct for simplicity over complexity in all matters.

Have experience in a growth-stage, product-oriented technology company and are energized by helping a lean team scale.

You can appreciate the whole distribution as much as a point estimator.

Put another way, you shouldn’t apply if:You are looking for a pure-management role removed from the details of analytical work. You will need to be comfortable getting hands-on as you learn the team and helping analysts work through difficult problems.

You have only worked in an environment where analysis begins after another team has fully prepared the data. Ashby analysts are expected to work across the stack, from modeling through final analysis and dashboards.

Spreadsheet-only analytical work is your preferred mode. Fluency with SQL in a modern data warehouse is essential.

You would rather use a metric, dashboard, experiment, or process by default than first ask what degree of evidence is actually needed to make a good decision.

You are looking for consumer-scale data infrastructure projects. We have a large and interesting dataset (see our Talent Trends reports!), but we are a B2B SaaS company. Relative to many B2C services, we are small but mighty.

You are seeking an in-person work experience. Ashby is remote, although there are employee hotspots around the world and we meet in person at various events throughout the year.

You have never formally managed a data team.

Naturally, this role is important and represents a combination of different skills. You may not meet every dimension perfectly, and that’s OK. If the dot product of your skill vector with this requirements vector is close to 1, please consider applying, but please note it does not have to be 1.0.


Data Culture at AshbyAt Ashby, we draw a clear distinction between when to look to data for "the answer" and when to use data to aid principled thinking for decision making. In general, a primary consideration is whether or not data is needed to help clarify points of uncertainty. When data is considered necessary, a secondary consideration is to what depth data will be required. Data questions lend themselves to ongoing "what about..." or "what if..." explorations, which can be important in some situations but are not always necessary.

With these dynamics in mind, we do not foster an environment where every decision we make should be backed by data, but we do foster an environment where teammates ask whether or not data will fit the task at hand well. This, in turn, allows us to operate a lean team focused on projects where data provides true leverage to our overall business and product goals.

As a related but distinct point, Ashby’s data culture, as far as transparency and access goes, is very open. We share company-wide access to our financial standings, progress, goals, and generally make any data and reporting results broadly available. Outside of constraints related to whether a teammate has access to a particular tool, there are close to no constraints on access the state of the company as told by data or reporting. In general, we would like to continue and extend open access to data throughout the company (with your help!), but with consideration and not as a substitute for principled thinking :)



Interview ProcessOur interview process is thorough, but we aim to be respectful of the total candidate time invested. We aim to ensure each person that joins the team is the right fit for Ashby and will provide ample information for you to determine if Ashby is the right fit for you. The expected process for this role is as follows:

Hiring Manager Screen (30 mins)

Technical Screen (45 min)

Assessment: Mini Analysis and Write-up (45min)

Final Round - Virtual Onsite (~2.5, can be split into multiple days)

(45 mins) Data Team: Analysis and Productivity

(45 mins) Data Team: Analysis and Collaboration

(30 mins) Business Partnership

(30 mins) Chat with a Founder

(15 mins) Follow-Up Conversation + Debrief with the Hiring Manager

Note: please do not reach out to the broader Ashby team requesting more information or time to connect. We will diligently review all applications in detail after the public posting period is over.


BenefitsCompetitive salary and equity.

10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby - do it when you feel financially comfortable.

Unlimited PTO, and we will encourage you to take it.

A minimum of 12 weeks of fully paid parental leave, covered by Ashby. For folks outside the US, it may be longer to be in line with regional requirements.

Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

$100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

If you’re in the US, we offer top-tier health insurance for you and your dependents, with 100% of premiums covered by Ashby. In other countries, we provide high-quality supplemental health insurance for you and your dependents, also fully covered by us.

Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply.


If you've made it this far and are excited about Ashby, please apply and follow us on LinkedIn to stay up to date!

Ashby provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

Ashby is committed to a fair and transparent hiring process. We confirm that this advertisement is for an active, existing vacancy within our organization. Please be advised that we may use artificial intelligence-driven tools to assist our recruitment team in screening, assessing, and selecting candidates for this position.

About Monster Energy: Forget about blending in. That's not our style. We're the risk-takers, the trailblazers, the game-changers. We're not perfect, and we don't pretend to be. We're raw, unfiltered, and a bit unconventional. But our drive is unrivaled, just like our athletes. The power is in your hands to define what success looks like and where you want to take your career. It's not just about what we do, but about who we become along the way. We are much more than a brand here. We are a way of life, a mindset. Join us. 

A Day in the Life:In the role of International Digital Analytics Manager, you’ll fuel the international digital growth of Monster’s diverse brand portfolio, transforming data into actionable strategies that power performance across web, social, paid media, search, and promotions. You’ll support the Analytics Director in defining the roadmap and designing impactful measurement frameworks, unlocking consumer insights, and implementing best-in-class analytics solutions that drive smarter marketing decisions and accelerate brand for international markets.

The Impact You'll Make:Analyze performance across paid social, online video, programmatic, CTV (Connected TV) , search, websites, organic social, creators, CRM (Customer Relationship Management), and eCommerce. Integrate additional media and commercial data where available to provide a comprehensive view of marketing effectiveness. Act as a data storyteller by creating dashboards and presentations that effectively convey actionable insights for technical and non-technical audiences.Use Tealium or equivalent CDP (Customer Data Platform) solutions to analyze first-party data and develop audience segments based on consumer behavior, engagement, and lifecycle stage.   Join TeamHealth in a highly visible finance leadership role supporting one of the organization's largest and most complex business groups!

description: Risepoint is an education technology company that helps regional universities launch and grow online programs for modern learners. Risepoint supports more than 100 universities and colleges across five countries, with programs concentrated in high-demand fields including nursing, healthcare, teaching, business, technology, and public service. Our suite of products and services supports the full student journey and each university’s long-term goals. Together, we increase access to affordable education that delivers a strong return on investment for learners and meets employer and community needs. Learn more at risepoint.com. About This Opportunity Risepoint partners with leading universities to expand access to high-quality online education, and Partner Strategy & Analytics team sits at the center of how those partnerships grow and perform. We're looking for a Marketing & Operations Analytics Manager who can turn complex, full-funnel partner data — from lead generation through yield — into the strategic narrative that shapes how Risepoint invests in and grows its portfolio of partner institutions. This role is built for someone who thrives at the intersection of rigorous analysis and cross-functional leadership. You'll own analytical workstreams end-to-end, from framing the right question to delivering the insight that moves a decision, while partnering closely with Integrated Marketing, Channel Marketing, Partner Management, and Operations teams. You'll be expected to spot the data quality issue before it becomes a stakeholder problem, build the pipelines that make partner performance monitoring reliable, and use AI-assisted tools like Claude and Databricks Genie to work faster without ever outsourcing your judgment. As the team grows, you'll also start building and coaching the analysts around you — this is a role with real room to grow into people leadership. If you want a seat where your analysis directly informs how a national portfolio of university partnerships is managed and grown, this is that seat. The Impact You Will Make You'll be the analytical backbone behind partner growth strategy. Your work on enrollment funnel performance — lead gen through yield — will directly shape the conversations and decisions that determine how Risepoint supports long-term partner growth. You'll protect the integrity of the data leadership relies on. By catching errors, discontinuities, and reconciliation gaps before they surface downstream, you'll build a level of trust in the numbers that lets stakeholders move faster and with more confidence. You'll build infrastructure that outlasts any single analysis. The pipelines and reporting workflows you design — in partnership with BI and data engineering — will become the foundation partner performance monitoring runs on well beyond your own day-to-day work. You'll set the pace for how the team works. description:
Who we are 

At Twilio, we're shaping the future of communications, all from the comfort of our homes. We deliver innovative solutions to hundreds of thousands of businesses and empower millions of developers worldwide to craft personalized customer experiences.

Our dedication to remote-first work, and strong culture of connection and global inclusion means that no matter your location, you're part of a vibrant team with diverse experiences making a global impact each day. As we continue to revolutionize how the world interacts, we're acquiring new skills and experiences that make work feel truly rewarding. Your career at Twilio is in your hands.  
.

Hiring and how we work

We use Artificial Intelligence (AI) to help make our hiring process efficient. That said, every hiring decision is made by real Twilions! 

Also, while we are a remote-first company, you may be asked to report in person on an ad-hoc basis for team gatherings, functional off-sites or customer meetings.   
.

See yourself at Twilio

Join the team as Twilio's next Sr. Marketing Strategy and Analytics Manager, Social Impact.

About the job

Twilio.org is seeking a Sr. Marketing Strategy and Analytics Manager to serve as the dedicated operational business partner to our Social Impact marketing leadership. Sitting at the intersection of Go-To-Market (GTM) Strategy, marketing operations, and advanced data modeling, you won't just report on what happened, you will design the automation, attribution, and account prioritization engines that drive what happens next. This is an ideal opportunity for:

  * The Analytics Strategist ready to drive decisions: You have deep technical data chops (SQL, Python, modeling) but want to move beyond reporting to directly author investment proposals, influence leadership, and see your analyses translate into decisions being made.
  * The Specialized Marketer ready for full-lifecycle ownership: You have deep subject-matter expertise in one domain (such as demand generation, marketing ops, or lifecycle marketing) and are ready to expand your runway to own the entire marketing engine, from top-of-funnel triggers and budget allocation to field event ROI and executive scorecards.



Responsibilities

In this role, you'll:

  * Act as Strategic GTM Business Partner: Drive regular operating rhythms, quarterly pipeline generation (PG) OKR targets, QBR data packs, and marketing budget allocation frameworks alongside marketing leadership.
  * Lead Investment Proposals & Impact Modeling: Architect rigorous business cases, scenario models, and ROI forecasts to secure investment for new marketing programs; evaluate capital trade-offs across channels and stress-test the expected pipeline return and payback periods before launch.
  * Lead Pipeline Automation & Marketing Triggers: Design, script, and operationalize automated marketing triggers in Python/SQL notebooks to power high-converting marketing plays and feed targeted accounts directly into sales workflows.
  * Architect Attribution & Single Source of Truth: Own end-to-end pipeline attribution models across sales, marketing, and partner channels; maintain rep-level marketing metrics integrated directly into Frontline Manager (FLM) data packs and leadership scorecards.
  * Drive Account Tiering & Routing: Operationalize advanced account tiering and segmentation logic across Salesforce (SFDC) and 6sense/Segment to optimize lead routing, demand generation campaigns, and Account-Based Marketing (ABM) outreach.
  * Advanced Commercial Modeling: Partner with broader central data science teams on company wide marketing frameworks (like Marketing Mix Modeling), while independently owning custom scenario analysis (e.g., ASP impact of bundling, Customer Lifetime Value/LFTV cohorting, and field event ROI modeling).
  * Maintain & Modernize GTM Data Infrastructure: Curate and optimize our Looker, Tableau, and SFDC reporting assets, managing SQL logic via GitHub version control, dashboard glossaries, and automated data QA processes.



Qualifications 

Twilio values diverse experiences from all kinds of industries, and we encourage everyone who meets the required qualifications to apply. If your career is just starting or hasn't followed a traditional path, don't let that stop you from considering Twilio. We are always looking for people who will bring something new to the table!

*Required:

  * 5+ years of experience in Marketing Analytics, GTM Strategy, Revenue Operations, or Business Intelligence within a high-growth B2B SaaS or technology organization.
  * Advanced Technical Stack: Mastery of complex SQL and proficiency in Python (or R) for data extraction, manipulation, statistical analysis, and pipeline automation.
  * Data Visualization & BI: Proven track record building enterprise-grade executive scorecards and self-serve dashboards in Tableau and Looker.
  * CRM & GTM Tech Stack Depth: Strong functional understanding of Salesforce (SFDC) data architecture, campaign hierarchies, lead routing rules, and marketing automation platforms.
  * Commercial Acumen & Executive Presence: Exceptional communication skills with demonstrated experience partnering directly with Director/VP-level leaders to turn data insights into operational decisions.



Desired:

  * Experience working with customer data platforms and intent tools (e.g., Segment, 6sense, Marketo).
  * Experience with Marketing Modeling, multi-touch attribution, and lifetime value (CLV/LFTV) analyses.
  * Familiarity with Git/GitHub workflows for analytics version control.
  * Genuine passion or prior experience in the social impact, non-profit, or public sector technology domains.



Location

This role will be remote, but is not eligible to be hired in CA, CT, NJ, NY, PA, WA.

Travel 

We prioritize connection and opportunities to build relationships with our customers and each other. For this role, approximately 15% travel is anticipated to help you connect in-person in a meaningful way. 

What We Offer

Working at Twilio offers many benefits, including competitive pay, generous time off, ample parental and wellness leave, healthcare, a retirement savings program, and much more. Offerings vary by location.

Compensation

*Please note this role is open to candidates outside of California, Colorado, Hawaii, Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts, Minnesota, New Jersey, New York, Vermont, Washington D.C., and Washington State. The information below is provided for candidates hired in those locations only.

The estimated pay ranges for this role are as follows:

  * Based in Colorado, Hawaii, Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Vermont or Washington D.C. : $128,560 - $160,700.
  * Based in New York, New Jersey, Washington State, or California (outside of the San Francisco Bay area): $136,000 - $170,000.
  * Based in the San Francisco Bay area, California: $151,120 - $188,900.
  * This role may be eligible to participate in Twilio's equity plan and corporate bonus plan. All roles are generally eligible for the following benefits: health care insurance, 401(k) retirement account, paid sick time, paid personal time off, paid parental leave.



The successful candidate's starting salary will be determined based on permissible, non-discriminatory factors such as skills, experience, and geographic location.

Application deadline information (required for ALL US jobs)

Applications for this role are intended to be accepted until October 31, 2026, but may change based on business needs. 

Twilio thinks big. Do you?

We like to solve problems, take initiative, pitch in when needed, and are always up for trying new things. That's why we seek out colleagues who embody our values — something we call Twilio Magic. Additionally, we empower employees to build positive change in their communities by supporting their volunteering and donation efforts.

So, if you're ready to unleash your full potential, do your best work, and be the best version of yourself, apply now! If this role isn't what you're looking for, please consider other open positions.

.

Stay alert to recruitment fraud

We care about your safety. Scammers sometimes impersonate Twilio recruiters through fake job postings, emails, websites, or messages. Please ensure you are engaging with an official @twilio.com email address. We will never ask for payment, gift cards, cryptocurrency, or banking information during the recruiting process. We do not make job offers without a formal interview process or conduct interviews exclusively through text-based messaging apps.  
  
.

Twilio is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, reproductive health decisions, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, genetic information, political views or activity, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law. Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers and the California Fair Chance Act. Additionally, Twilio participates in the E-Verify program in certain locations, as required by law.

Are you someone who loves turning data into insights, solving problems, and building strong client relationships?


MBMS is looking for a Client Analytics Manager (CAM) who can do more than analyze numbers—you’ll use data, communication, and business insight to help our healthcare clients make smarter decisions and improve their financial performance.


As a Client Analytics Manager, you’ll serve as a trusted advisor and strategic partner to our clients. You’ll work closely with healthcare practices to understand their challenges, identify opportunities, translate complex information into meaningful insights, and help deliver solutions that make a measurable difference.


This is an ideal opportunity for someone who enjoys a combination of analytics, healthcare, client consulting, relationship management, and problem-solving.


What You’ll Do


Be a Trusted Client Partner



 Build strong, lasting relationships with healthcare practices and their leadership teams.
 Serve as a knowledgeable, responsive resource and advocate for your clients.
 Meet with clients to discuss performance, challenges, opportunities, and industry trends.
 Present financial and operational insights in a way that is clear, meaningful, and actionable.
 Identify opportunities to enhance services and create additional value for clients.

Turn Data Into Strategy



 Analyze revenue cycle and month-end financial results.
 Identify trends in revenue, payer mix, procedure mix, charges, and other key performance indicators.
 Develop revenue projections and cash-flow analyses.
 Benchmark client performance against comparable organizations and industry data.
 Conduct carrier impact analyses and annual fee schedule reviews.
 Develop recommendations based on your findings.

Solve Problems & Identify Opportunities



 Proactively identify client challenges, opportunities, and potential threats.
 Partner with internal teams to develop practical solutions.
 Communicate significant issues proactively, including the cause, expected timeframe, financial impact, resolution plan, and prevention strategies.
 Facilitate special projects and initiatives that improve client outcomes.
 Bring forward ideas that can improve services for both individual clients and MBMS as a whole.

Build Reporting & Business Intelligence



 Prepare monthly, quarterly, and year-end financial reporting packages.
 Develop ad-hoc reports and analyses based on client needs.
 Create meaningful dashboards and visualizations using Microsoft Power BI.
 Utilize advanced Excel capabilities, including formulas, pivot tables, and charts.
 Support data validation and integrity.
 Help streamline reporting and develop new KPIs, measures, aggregations, and dynamic visualizations.
 Provide training to internal and external teams on reporting tools.

Support Payer Contract Analysis



 Partner with the Contract Variance Manager to review third-party payer contracts.
 Analyze contract terms and fee schedules.
 Monitor reimbursement and audit payments against contracted rates.
 Communicate findings and opportunities to clients

Stay Ahead of Healthcare Trends


You’ll be expected to stay informed about changes and trends affecting the healthcare industry, revenue cycle management, reimbursement, and medical practice operations—and bring that knowledge to your client relationships.


What We’re Looking For


We’re looking for someone who is:



 Analytical – You enjoy digging into data and finding the story behind the numbers.
 Client-focused – You understand that great service is about anticipating needs, not simply responding to requests.
 A strong communicator – You can explain complex information clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
 A problem solver – You naturally look for solutions and opportunities for improvement.
 Confident and collaborative – You’re comfortable working directly with clients, vendors, and internal teams.
 Curious – You enjoy learning about healthcare, industry trends, technology, and business strategy.
 Organized – You can manage multiple clients, projects, deadlines, and priorities.
 Adaptable – You are comfortable learning new technologies and adjusting as business needs evolve.

Skills & Experience


Preferred qualifications include:



 Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including formulas, pivot tables, and charts.
 Experience with Power BI or similar business intelligence/visualization platforms.
 Experience working with data analytics, financial reporting, or revenue cycle information.
 Strong presentation and client relationship skills.
 Ability to analyze trends and translate findings into actionable recommendations.
 Bachelor’s degree preferred.
 Healthcare, medical billing, revenue cycle, practice management, or analytics experience is a plus.

Professional certifications such as CMPE, CHBME, or CHDA are valued but are not required.


A Role With Real Client Impact


At MBMS, the Client Analytics Manager isn’t simply a reporting role.


You’ll have the opportunity to sit at the intersection of data, healthcare, technology, and client strategy.


Your insights can help practices understand their financial performance, identify opportunities, address challenges, and make better business decisions.


You’ll also collaborate across MBMS teams including Client Services, Operations, Coding, Credentialing, MIPS, and Marketing/Development, giving you exposure to a broad range of healthcare business functions.

Physical Requirements



 Prolonged periods of sitting and working at a computer.
 Ability to lift up to 15 pounds occasionally.

Why This Role?


Analytics + Healthcare + Client Strategy + Relationship Building


If you enjoy working with data but don’t want to spend your entire day behind a spreadsheet—and you enjoy working with people, solving problems, and making an impact—this could be the role for you.

title: Automation Engineer
description:
Who We Are 
Spectro Cloud is the Kubernetes and AI infrastructure platform behind some of the most demanding AI environments in the world. Our PaletteAI platform, AI Inference Launchpad, and Instinct Coder solutions let operators stand up production-grade AI clusters — training, fine tuning, and inference — on any GPU, in any data center, at any scale. NeoClouds and specialty GPU cloud providers are one of the fastest-growing segments in the AI economy, and Spectro Cloud is the platform layer they trust to bring differentiated, multi-tenant, GPU-native services to market. 

About the Job
As an AI Automation Engineer, you will be part of internal efforts to advance AI adoption across the company. You will design, build, and maintain internally focused solutions that help promote agentic workflows and automations that improve employee productivity. 

This role will require you to wear different hats; one moment you are building a technical solution, and the next you may be engaging with risk, compliance, and legal to help define guardrails for a product or tool rollout. You will lead proof-of-concept initiatives, engage with employees during AI Office Hours to provide advice, and work with our internal partners to establish AI processes and guardrails. You must be comfortable teaching and explaining ideas to non-technical audiences. 

You are expected to have experience with various AI/ML workflows and AI development practices, primarily to advise, but also to shape the future of our products. We are an infrastructure-focused software company, so you are expected to have a strong understanding of infrastructure, spanning cloud and bare-metal environments. You should be comfortable creating automation solutions, with and without AI, that help us promote effective AI usage within the company. Experience deploying and managing applications in production will help you propose and build sustainable solutions.

We are seeking self-starters eager to help shape the future of this new team. We’re looking for someone who isn't afraid to share recommendations and guidance on AI initiatives and AI adoption within an organization. We face several unknowns that we must tackle together. If you enjoy working in a highly technical environment with autonomy, at a rapid pace, and with regular challenges, then this role is right for you. 

Minimum Qualifications
We don’t expect the ideal candidate to check every box, but the items below are things we look for when reviewing candidates. Do not let this discourage you from applying. 


● Bachelor's Degree or an Advanced Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a similar field.
● 4+ years of experience as a Software Engineer, SRE, ML Engineer, Solutions Architect, or similar technical role is required 
● 4+ years of experience maintaining and building production applications. 
● Possesses a broad knowledge and experience across AI topics, including agent based systems, model tuning, model deployment, MCP server development, and more. 
● Highly proficient with at least one of the following programming languages: Python, Go, or JavaScript/TypeScript (We prefer Go)
● Experience with application testing and continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD). This will come into play as you build and maintain solutions the AI team will own and support. 
● Project management experience. You are capable of leading and driving projects, such as proof-of-concept and the rollout of a new technical solution organization-wide. 
● Excellent communication skills, both written and oral. You will be expected to participate and lead office hours. You must be able to articulate technical concepts to engineers, non-engineers, and executives. 
● Experience with Infrastructure as Code, preferably Terraform. 
● Experience with public cloud providers (AWS, Azure, GCP, Oracle), and on-prem infrastructure. 
● Deep understanding of containers and how container orchestration systems work, such as Kubernetes.
● Displays a passion for learning and exploring new technologies 
● A self-starter with a strong sense of ownership 
● Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills, with a proactive approach to challenges 



The Hiring Process 
Your time is valuable, so we want to ensure we respect your time and the effort you put into the hiring process. The interview process is divided into four sections: a screening interview, a technical interview, and a culture and team fit interview. 
● Screening Interview—This is a thirty-minute interview during which we verify whether we are a good fit for each other. We’ll ask questions to learn more about your career experience. 
● Technical Interview - an hour interview where we verify your technical skills and knowledge. A take-home assignment is part of the interview and will be reviewed during the interview. 
● Culture/Team Interview—This is a thirty-minute interview. The questions here focus on your experience working in a team setting. Other questions check for organizational core values and culture fit.

Location This role can be worked from San Jose, CA or Austin, TX. We operate on a hybrid working model and are in the office 3 times a week, with optional WFH for the remainder of the week. Remote candidates can be considered, but preference will be given to individuals based in San Jose, CA or Austin, TX.

The total on-target earnings range for this role is between $160,000-192,000/year + Equity. Compensation will be based on experience and geographic market location.

Work Authorization/Visa: Applicants are required to be eligible to lawfully work in the U.S. immediately; employer is unable to sponsor applicants for U.S. work authorization for this opportunity.

Job Summary

At CBRE Global Workplace Solutions (GWS), Safety is our top priority! We maintain a safety-first culture in which CBRE employees return home in the same condition in which they reported to work. We're looking for a skilled and forward-thinking Ctrl Systems Engineer / Automation Engineer (AE) to join our growing team as we work to service one of the world's largest online retailers.

We offer competitive pay, robust benefits package, wellness programs, and a workplace environment that embraces diversity. Come join our global network of professionals supporting client operations across CBRE. Looking for growth and career advancement? Upon completing six months of successful service, associates may explore career advancement opportunities within the organization!

Read on to learn more!

About the Role

In this vital engineering role, you will be part of a team of controls and maintenance professionals who proactively support operations and provide customers with expert-level support based on the customer's technical problems related to their automated material handling equipment (MHE). Your expertise will be utilized in the continuous improvement and execution of the preventive maintenance process, with a focus on maximizing equipment reliability and operational performance of equipment such as conveyors, sortation systems, scanners, cameras, print and apply systems, SCADA deves and programs.

What You'll Do

Promote a safe working environment by complying with all applicable codes, regulations, governmental agencies, and company directives related to system operations and work safety.

Troubleshoot and modify software programs for material handling control systems, including PLC/PC controllers, Allen Bradley Controllogix/Compactlogix PLC platform and RSLogix 5000 software package.

Act as first level escalation in troubleshooting support, both on-site and remotely, as well as during and after business hours, to repair all MHE controls software systems. Respond quickly to emergency situations, summoning assistance as needed.

Inspect systems to ensure the operation of equipment is within design capabilities and achieves operational conditions prescribed by the client.

Oversee scope of development, work request initiation, scheduling, and inspection of work performed by outside contractors, which includes proprietary work, licensed installations, upgrades, and maintenance and inspection of specialized systems.

Engineer process solutions and reliability improvement from concept to network implementation.

Monitor Industrial networks such as Ethernet, ControlNet, DeviceNet, Profibus, AS-I, motor control systems, servo drives, frequency drives, and electrical distribution systems.

Monitor material handling equipment metrics and partner with site team to resolve equipment electrical problems that create performance deficiencies.

Proactively and effectively communicate with multiple stakeholders including, but not limited to, leadership, operations and the maintenance team on technical issues and project timelines and production impacts.

Facilitate analysis and reviews of failures and processes to provide recommendations to implement improvements or retraining to avoid future incidents.

Perform controls of systems assessments to maintain and improve equipment reliability.

Clearly communicate technical issues, project timelines, and product impacts with site leadership, operations and the maintenance teams.

Cultivate positive working relationships with our Client and the Operations Maintenance team members.

Perform other job-related duties as needed or assigned.

What You'll Need

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States without the need for visa sponsorship now or in the future.

Bachelor"s Degree preferred with 2-5 years of relevant experience. In lieu of a degree, a combination of experience and education may be considered.

Experience in at least two engineering design cycles including specification, component selection and programming.

2+ years of experience with Programmable Logic Controls (PLC) programs.

2+ years of experience with robotics system components and controls.

2+ years of experience with SCADA systems.

Ability to be available and work a flexible schedule/shift/work area, including weekends, nights, and/or holidays.

Ability to independently solve problems and carry out general instructions in standard situations with limited to no oversight.

Meet the physical requirements of this role including stooping, standing, walking, climbing stairs/ladders, and the ability to lift/carry heavy loads of 50 lbs. or more.

Ability to guide the exchange of sensitive, complicated, and difficult information, convey performance expectations, and handle problems.

Preferred Qualifications

2+ years apprenticeship or equivalent experience in Control Systems troubleshooting/ programming.

Experience supporting a range of different conveyors and sortation systems.

Experience with robotic maintenance.

In-depth knowledge of Microsoft Office products. Examples include Word, Excel, Outlook, etc.

Extensive organizational skills with a strong inquisitive mindset.

Advanced math skills. Ability to calculate difficult figures such as percentages, fractions, and other financial-related calculations.

description:
The Automation Engineer III - Temporary serves as the senior technical authority responsible for leading the design, configuration, integration, and lifecycle management of process control, automation, and industrial IT/OT systems across Manufacturing, Quality Control, Analytical, and Process Development operations. Located in College Station, TX, this role balances hands-on technical troubleshooting with strategic leadership, project execution, and cross-functional collaboration to ensure reliability, efficiency, and strict regulatory compliance in a biopharmaceutical setting. The position also provides technical mentorship to junior automation engineers.

Responsibilities:
Technical Leadership & Lifecycle Management: Provide hands-on leadership for the design, configuration, integration, qualification, and lifecycle management of control systems across plant and lab operations.   
System Troubleshooting & Root Cause Analysis: Lead advanced troubleshooting for process control systems???including PLC, DCS, SCADA, and equipment-level automation???to support uninterrupted GMP operations.   
Project Execution & Qualification: Manage automation project implementations, requirement definitions, and vendor coordination while supporting commissioning and qualification (IQ/OQ/PQ) activities.   
Compliance & Data Integrity: Ensure system configurations, electronic records, and audit trails comply with GxP, 21 CFR Part 11, and ALCOA+ data integrity standards.   
Client Programs & Tech Transfer: Support tech transfer activities, client program customizations, client meetings, and regulatory inspections/audits.   
Continuous Improvement: Identify and execute continuous improvement initiatives to optimize system reliability, scalability, and operational efficiency within a CDMO environment.   
Mentorship: Offer technical guidance, coaching, and mentorship to junior automation engineers to build capability and promote engineering standardization.

Working hours: 8:00 AM - 5:00 PM

Skills:
Education & Experience: Bachelor's degree in Engineering (Chemical, Electrical, Mechanical, Computer, or related) with 6-12+ years of automation/process control/OT experience in biopharmaceutical or regulated manufacturing.   
Automation Platform Expertise: Demonstrated design, implementation, and lifecycle management skills in DCS, PLC, SCADA, and HMI platforms (e.g., DeltaV, Rockwell/Allen-Bradley, Siemens).   
Regulatory & Validation Compliance: In-depth working knowledge of FDA regulations (21 CFR Parts 210/211 and Part 11), ALCOA+ data integrity, Computerized System Validation (CSV), GAMP 5, and ISA-88/ISA-95 frameworks.   
Commissioning & Qualification: Hands-on experience executing IQ/OQ/PQ validation protocols, deviation management, CAPA, and change control within GMP environments.   
Bioprocessing Equipment: Experience supporting bioprocess systems such as single-use bioreactors, filtration (TFF), and chromatography systems.   
OT/IT & Industrial Networking: Proficiency in OT asset management in Windows environments, Active Directory (AD) integration, industrial network architecture (switches, firewalls, VLANs), and cybersecurity principles (e.g., NIST, ISA/IEC 62443).   
Problem-Solving & Soft Skills: Excellent root cause analysis abilities, communication, documentation, and the capacity to balance hands-on work with strategic initiatives in a lean organization.

description:
Since 1892, OPW customers have been able to count on us to revolutionize fluid-handling operations around the world. As a global leader in fluid-handling solutions, the mission of OPW is to be a developer of a comprehensive array of innovative fluid-handling solutions that our customers can consistently and reliably count on. These include loading and unloading systems for high-value hazardous and non-hazardous bulk products; railcar and transport tank-truck valves, gauging devices and tank-monitoring systems; automated storage-terminal controls and systems; and regulators, fittings, valves, vaporizers, vacuum-jacketed piping and gas-handling systems for the safe handling and distribution of cryogenics and industrial gases. OPW has more than 2,000 employees with manufacturing operations in North America, Europe and China, and sales offices around the world. OPW is part of the Clean Energy & Fueling segment of Dover (NYSE: DOV).



 

 The Automation Engineer will be responsible for the design, programming, integration, troubleshooting, and continuous improvement of automated assembly and testing equipment, including PLC-controlled machinery, robotic work cells, and associated controls hardware. This role will work cross-functionally with manufacturing engineering, maintenance, quality, and production teams to bring automated systems from concept through commissioning (both in-house and vendor) and provide ongoing production support. We are looking for individuals who have knowledge or experience in assembly/testing and automation processes, a keen eye for safety and quality, the ability to solve problems and troubleshoot, and the desire to develop and expand their skills in a production-driven environment. The Automation Engineer will report to the PES Value Stream Manager.



 


 

 

 What You'll Do 


 Controls Design and Programming 


 
  Design, develop, and debug PLC programs (Allen-Bradley, Siemens, or similar) for assembly automation equipment
  Program and integrate industrial robots (FANUC, Universal Robots, etc.) for pick-and-place, path planning, material handling, loading/unloading, dispensing, welding, or assembly applications
  Develop HMI screens and operator interfaces for machine control and diagnostics
  Design and implement vision system integration (Keyence or similar) for part inspection, guidance, and quality verification
  Configure and troubleshoot servo motion control systems, VFDs, and motor drivesCollaborate with mechanical and electrical design engineers during the concept and design phases to ensure controls feasibility
 
 

 Equipment Specification & Vendor Management 


 
  Develop detailed technical specifications (URS/equipment specs) for new automation equipment, including PLC, robotics, and vision system requirements
  Research and evaluate automation equipment vendors, integrators, and component suppliers based on technical fit, cost, lead time, and reliability
  Solicit and review vendor quotes and proposals; lead technical evaluation and vendor selection process
  Manage vendor-built automation projects from kickoff through FAT/SAT and installation, including schedule tracking, budget oversight, and change order management
  Review vendor-supplied design packages, electrical schematics, and controls documentation for compliance with internal standards and specifications
  Act as primary technical point of contact and lead design reviews, progress meetings, and FAT/SAT activities with external vendors and integratorsEnsure vendor equipment meets safety, quality, and performance requirements prior to acceptance and handoff to production
 
 

 Troubleshooting & Continuous Improvement 


 
  Provide technical support for installed equipment, including root cause analysis and corrective action for downtime events
  Identify and implement improvements to improve machine uptime, cycle time, and overall equipment effectiveness (OEE)
  Support preventive maintenance programs and develop troubleshooting documentation for maintenance and production staff
  Analyze production data and machine performance to identify optimization opportunitiesIntegrate mechanical, electrical, pneumatic, and controls subsystems into functioning automated work cells
 
 
Documentation & Compliance 


 
  Create and maintain electrical schematics, I/O lists, controls architecture diagrams, and program documentation that complies with all applicable safety standards
  Participate in risk assessments and safety validation for automated equipmentMaintain version control and backups of PLC, HMI, and robot programs
 
 


 

 

 What You'll Bring 


 
  Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, Mechatronics, Controls Engineering, or a related field
  3+ years of experience programming and troubleshooting PLCs in an industrial/manufacturing environment
  Hands-on experience programming industrial robots and integrating them into automated systems
  Working knowledge of electrical schematics, ladder logic, structured text, and function block programming
  Understanding of pneumatics, sensors (photo eyes, proximity, encoders), servo/motion control, and machine safety circuits
  Experience with HMI development platforms
  Strong troubleshooting skills with the ability to diagnose mechanical, electrical, and software issues under time pressure
  Ability to read and interpret mechanical drawings, electrical schematics, and P&IDsAdvanced knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite
 
 

 The Ideal Candidate Will Also Bring 


 
  Experience with FANUC and Universal Robots programming/certification
  Familiarity with machine vision systems (Keyence or similar)
  Experience with industrial networking protocols (EtherNet/IP, Profinet, DeviceNet, Modbus TCP)
  Experience with Autodesk Inventor, SolidWorks, or similar 3D CAD software for reviewing mechanical designs
  Prior experience in high-volume assembly and testing automation, packaging automation, or similarSix Sigma, Lean Manufacturing, or continuous improvement training

description:
**Job Description:**

**Company:** Oliver Wyman

**Who we are**

Oliver Wyman is a global management consulting firm. We work with clients through their most defining moments, combining deep industry knowledge, specialized expertise, and the power of perspective to help them adapt, grow, and thrive. We believe diverse perspectives make the work stronger. Our consultants bring different backgrounds, experiences, and ways of thinking to help solve complex problems and create lasting impact for clients, colleagues, and communities. At Oliver Wyman, we are proud of the values that we aspire to live by. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive and reach their full potential.

Within Oliver Wyman, the Data & Analytics (DNA) division was established in 2017 and operates globally, with a particular focus on Europe. We are a dynamic and rapidly growing team of quantitative analytics specialists, collaborating closely with colleagues across the firm. Our work spans multiple industries, including Financial Services, Climate & Sustainability, Energy, Retail, and Transportation.

**What you will do**

As a member of Oliver Wyman’s Data & Analytics team, you will help clients make better decisions on some of their most important business challenges. You will combine analytical thinking, business understanding, and technical expertise to develop solutions that are both rigorous and practical. You will contribute throughout the project lifecycle: structuring the client’s problem, identifying the decisions that analysis needs to support, assessing the available data, and selecting an appropriate analytical approach. You will conduct analyses, build and validate models or tools, and translate the results into clear recommendations. As you develop, you will take increasing ownership of analytical modules and engage directly with clients and senior colleagues. You will also be an active member of the project team: sharing your ideas, discussing results with colleagues and clients, and helping turn analytical findings into meaningful recommendations and impact.

Examples of the work you could contribute to include:

- Building an AI toolkit to predict credit rating downgrades from news articles.

- Modeling portfolio decarbonization strategies for European banks.

- Optimizing promotions for an Asian health & beauty chain using advanced analytics.

- Validating a customer-facing Gen. AI chatbot for a bank.

- Designing credit risk models in Python for banks in Europe.

- Identifying supply chain risks using live data and AI.

**Why join us?**

You can be your best here. At Oliver Wyman, you will find meaningful work, talented people, and a culture built on trust, support, and growth.

**Create solutions that have impact**

Work on challenging projects that help clients solve complex analytical problems, make better decisions, and create meaningful impact. Contribute to tailored Data & Analytics solutions across industries and geographies, applying analytical approaches to real client challenges. Be part of teams that measure success not just by deliverables, but by the difference created together.

**Develop as a leader**

From day one, be encouraged to take initiative, ask questions, and bring your perspective to the work. Work alongside colleagues and clients at different levels, contributing your ideas and developing confidence through hands-on experience. Build the skills to communicate complex analytical concepts clearly and contribute effectively to client and team discussions.

**Learn without limits**

Expect a steep learning curve, as no two projects are the same. Expand your analytical and technical toolkit through exposure to a variety of challenges, industries, and technologies. Learn from experienced colleagues throughout your career, supported by a dedicated buddy, career adviser, and talent manager. Gain international exposure through opportunities to work across different cultures and, where projects require it, travel internationally.

**Thrive in a vibrant and inclusive culture**

Work with genuine colleagues who collaborate across differences and support one another. Be part of an open and inclusive environment where diverse perspectives, backgrounds, and experiences strengthen the work. Bring your curiosity, share your ideas, and contribute to a collaborative team that values different ways of thinking.

**Experience rewards that work for you**

Build your career in an environment that supports both professional growth and sustainable work-life quality. Benefit from flexibility designed to help you balance your career aspirations with your personal life. Have the support and resources you need to keep learning, growing, and performing at your best.

**Who can apply?**

- Bachelor’s, Master’s, or Ph. D degree in a quantitative discipline (e.g., Data Science, Mathematics, Natural Sciences, Statistics, Computer Science, Engineering), with a strong academic track record.

- A data-driven mindset and proficiency with numbers, paired with the ability to explain sophisticated data science concepts in an understandable manner to clients and colleagues.

- Proficiency in at least one programming language, either Python or R, combined with an eagerness to continuously expand your knowledge of technologies and analytical methods.

- Strong commitment to teamwork and resilience in a creative, dynamic, and constantly changing environment.

- Willingness to travel and work on-site with clients as required.

- Language skills: business fluency in German and English.

- Interest in or experience with financial services and risk management is a plus.

**How to apply?**

Please submit your CV, cover letter, all employment references, and academic transcripts (including your high school diploma, Bachelor's degree, and Master's degree). If you would like to learn more about Oliver Wyman, please visit our website or, alternatively, apply to attend one of our events, details of which can be found here.

**What to expect during the interview process?**

At Oliver Wyman, we want you to shine in your interview. Our process is designed like our work environment - it’s challenging, exciting, and fun. With a mix of conversational and case interviews, our approach not only helps us get to know you better and understand your strengths and interests but also enables you to learn more about our people and our business. If you want to learn more about our case interviews and start your preparation, please visit our careers page.

Oliver Wyman is a business of Marsh (NYSE: MRSH), a global leader in risk, reinsurance and capital, people and investments, and management consulting, advising clients in 130 countries. With annual revenue of over $27 billion and more than 95,000 colleagues, Marsh helps build the confidence to thrive through the power of perspective. For more information, visit oliverwyman.com, or follow us on Linked. In and X.

Marsh is committed to creating a diverse, inclusive and flexible work environment. We aim to attract and retain the best people and embrace diversity of age, background, disability, ethnic origin, family duties, gender orientation or expression, marital status, nationality, parental status, personal or social status, political affiliation, race, religion and beliefs, sex/gender, sexual orientation or expression, skin color, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Marsh offers hybrid working arrangements that provide both the flexibility of mobile working and the benefits for collaboration, personal connections and professional development of working in the office. Employees are authorized to work remotely. If needed, some teams also schedule weekly “anchor days” where the entire team meets in person at the site office.

title: Master Data Management Consultant III
description:
Position Summary:   

The Master Data Management Consultant III is responsible for enterprise master data management across the financial, organizational, material, asset, and business partner domains, establishing the data standards, quality rules, and stewardship practices that allow financial and logistics information to reconcile without manual intervention, in support of a large-scale, greenfield SAP S/4HANA financial management modernization program for a Department of War (DoW) organization. The consultant independently owns assigned master data domains, leads stewardship and data quality sessions for that scope, and resolves moderately complex harmonization and duplication issues across legacy sources. This position operates at Level III of the C5MI job architecture and contributes to delivery across a five-gate milestone structure spanning pre-design approval, preliminary design review, critical design review, production readiness review, and closeout. 

Note:  This position is contingent upon contract award. 

 

Essential Functions and Responsibilities: 

Owns assigned master data domains, including attribute definition, business rules, valid value sets, and domain-specific data quality thresholds. Designs and implements match, merge, and survivorship rules to establish authoritative records from multiple legacy sources, and resolves conflicting source data; where SAP Master Data Governance is the enforcement platform, this includes consolidation and mass processing rule design. Defines and maintains data quality rules, measures, and scorecards; analyzes data quality trends and drives remediation with data stewards and functional owners. Leads stewardship working sessions with business data owners to establish ownership, approval paths, and remediation accountability for assigned domains. Designs master data lifecycle processes, including creation, change, extension, blocking, and marking-for-deletion, and the controls applied at each transition. Supports cross-domain consistency analysis, ensuring financial, material, asset, and organizational master data align to a single set of enterprise definitions. Handles moderately complex configuration and design work with minimal oversight, exercising judgment within established program design practices. Leads requirements gathering sessions and fit-to-standard workshops for assigned scope and documents the resulting functional designs and configuration rationale. Owns assigned deliverables end to end, including design, configuration, documentation, test execution, and defect resolution across unit, integration, and user acceptance testing. Mentors junior team members informally and reviews configuration and documentation produced within the assigned scope for quality and standards compliance. Supports authority to operate, cybersecurity, audit, and compliance activities associated with the program, including production of control evidence for assigned configuration. Supports cutover, go-live, and post-deployment hypercare activities for assigned scope, and contributes to transition of the delivered capability into the sustainment organization. Travels to client sites up to 50% to support workshops, design sessions, testing events, cutover, and go-live activities, varying based on client program schedules. Adheres to all certified processes as part of our commitment to maintaining the highest standards of quality and information security, which includes actively participating in quality assurance activities and ensuring the protection of sensitive information in accordance with our security policies. Performs other related tasks as assigned by direct supervisor.  

C5MI Expectations of all Employees: 

Adheres to all C5MI Policies and Procedures. Always conducts self in a manner consistent with C5MIs' Core Values. Maintains a positive and respectful attitude with all contacts. Consistently reports to work on time and prepared to perform the duties of the position. Meets productivity standards and performs duties as workload necessitates. Maintains the privacy of all company proprietary information. Treats vendors, customers, and team members with respect and dignity. Able to safely perform the essential functions of the job with or without reasonable accommodation.  

Minimum Qualifications: 

Bachelor's degree in a related field or equivalent experience; 3-5 years of relevant experience with a Bachelor's degree, or 5-7 years of relevant experience without a Bachelor's degree, including demonstrated experience owning deliverables and solving moderately complex problems. 3+ years of master data management or data governance experience in an enterprise environment. Demonstrated experience defining data quality rules, measures, and scorecards, and driving remediation with business data owners. Experience with match, merge, survivorship, and duplicate resolution across multiple source systems. Working knowledge of ERP master data domains and the downstream financial impact of master data defects. Proficiency with SQL or equivalent data analysis tooling. Ability to exercise judgment within defined practices and handle moderately complex issues with minimal oversight. Demonstrated experience owning deliverables through design, configuration, testing, and documentation. Experience supporting multi-system SAP landscapes. Secret security clearance required: must hold an active Secret clearance or be able to obtain and maintain one prior to assignment (requires U.S. citizenship).  

Nice to Have: 

Active Secret security clearance at time of hire. Experience supporting federal ERP modernization programs, Department of War (DoW) SAP environments, or other defense business systems acquired under DoDI 5000.75. Experience with SAP Master Data Governance as the enforcement platform for master data policy. Certified Data Management Professional (CDMP) or equivalent data management certification. Familiarity with federal financial audit drivers, including the Financial Improvement and Audit Readiness (FIAR) methodology, DoD 7000.14-R (Financial Management Regulation), and FFMIA. Experience aligning organizational master data to a force structure hierarchy or equivalent enterprise organizational data initiative. Experience with enterprise data catalog, lineage, or metadata management tooling. Compensation: In accordance with pay transparency law, the expected salary range for this position is $90,000-$105,000 annually. The actual compensation offered will be determined based on factors such as the candidate's experience, qualifications, skills, and location. We are committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. This posted range reflects our good faith estimate of the compensation we reasonably expect to offer for this role at the time of posting.

Application Deadline: We anticipate this job posting will be posted until 12/01/2026.

description:
Company OverviewWe are the better way to work in finance. As private equity’s value creation partner, we sit at the heart of PE—where sponsors and CFOs meet. Through financial consulting rooted in data, technology, and AI, we help clients drive value—supporting the office of the CFO to drive end-to-end value creation.

If you crave challenging work and are looking to grow, come solve complex issues alongside 1,600+ finance & technology experts in a supportive, collaborative environment.

Backed by premier private equity firms and headquartered in New York with 11 offices around the globe, we are a high-growth, entrepreneurial firm looking for people who want to be part of building something great. Come make your mark. 

Data & AnalyticsAccordion's Data & Analytics (D&A) team offers cutting-edge, intelligent solutions to a global clientele, leveraging a blend of domain knowledge, sophisticated technology tools, and deep analytics capabilities to tackle complex business challenges.

We partner with Private Equity clients and their Portfolio Companies across diverse sectors, including Retail, CPG, Healthcare, Media & Entertainment, Technology, and Logistics.

We deliver data and analytical solutions designed to streamline reporting capabilities and enhance business insights across vast and complex data sets ranging from Sales, Operations, Marketing, Pricing, Customer Strategies, and more.

This role can be based in any of our US office locations and is a hybrid role with the flexibility to work remotely 2 days a week. Ideal candidates should be local to the desired location.

This position is not eligible for immigration sponsorship.

About the Role and YouWe're looking for a rare combination: a data scientist who thinks like a strategist and a strategist who speaks fluent data. You fall in love with problems and quantify complex situations using math. This isn't a role about building models in isolation—it's about transforming how a business makes decisions, identifies opportunities, and drives growth. You'll be equal parts analyst, advisor, and architect of our strategic direction.

What You'll DoYou'll sit at the intersection of data and strategy, turning complex business challenges into quantifiable opportunities. This means diving deep into our numbers to surface insights that others miss, then translating those insights into actionable growth strategies. You'll work directly with leadership to shape major business decisions, from market expansion and pricing strategy to resource allocation and competitive positioning.Your day-to-day will involve identifying the right questions to ask before anyone else thinks to ask them, building the analytical frameworks to answer those questions, and presenting recommendations that fundamentally shift how we operate. You'll own strategic initiatives from conception through execution, measuring impact and iterating as you go. You’ll travel to client sites as needed, leading AI assessment and Strategy Engagements.

What We're Looking ForThe Strategic Mindset: You naturally think several moves ahead. You understand business models, competitive dynamics, and growth levers. You can walk into a room with executives and hold your own in discussions about market strategy, unit economics, and long-term planning. You've seen how businesses succeed and fail, and you know how to spot the difference.The Technical Depth: You're genuinely strong in quantitative methods—statistics, predictive modeling, optimization, experimental design. You can wrangle messy data, build robust analyses, and know when a sophisticated model is needed versus when a simple calculation will do. Python, R, SQL are still in your wheelhouse.The Translation Layer: You can explain complex analytical concepts to non-technical stakeholders without dumbing them down. You know how to build conviction around data-driven recommendations and can defend your methodology when challenged. You make the quantitative accessible and actionable.The Business Acumen: You understand P&Ls, growth metrics, customer economics, and operational levers. You've worked closely enough with business teams to know what keeps them up at night and how your analyses can help them sleep better.

Requirements5+ years of experience in analytical roles with increasing strategic responsibilityStrong foundation in statistics, machine learning, and quantitative analysisDemonstrated experience influencing business strategy through dataTrack record of identifying and driving growth opportunitiesExcellent communication skills with technical and executive audiencesProficiency in modern data science tools and languagesUnderstanding of business finance and growth frameworksIdeal BackgroundYou might come from management consulting with deep analytical chops, strategic roles at high-growth companies, corporate strategy teams with hands-on data work, or data science roles where you've grown into strategic advisory. What matters most is that you've successfully used data to change how businesses operate and grow.

What Success Looks LikeIn your first year, you'll have identified three major strategic opportunities we weren't seeing before, built the analytical infrastructure to evaluate them rigorously, and driven at least one to implementation with measurable business impact. You'll have become a trusted advisor to leadership and the person they turn to when facing the company's thorniest strategic questions.

Job Description

We are seeking a Big Data Engineer to design, build, and maintain real-time and near-realtime data ingestion pipelines supporting a mission-critical system and moves data across security domains using cross domain solutions (CDS) / guards. You will be responsible for the reliable flow of streaming data from a wide range of sources into our data platform, ensuring data quality, observability, and scalability.

You'll partner closely with data engineers, platform engineers, analytics teams, and security/governance personnel to deliver trustworthy, low-latency data that supports operational decisions - while ensuring compliance with cross-domain and data classification requirements. We're looking for a math teacher, tutor or statistician to check the formulas and worked solutions on the math calculators of KeenCalculator.com, a free calculator site with 430+ tools in 16 languages. You'll be credited by name as the reviewer of these pages.

PAGES TO REVIEW (English versions, 109 calculators in four categories)

- Math (44): https://keencalculator.com/math-calculators/

- Geometry (28): https://keencalculator.com/geometry-calculators/

- Statistics (22): https://keencalculator.com/statistics-calculators/

Each category page lists its calculators. Most are standard formulas (percentages, fractions, area and volume, mean and standard deviation, GPA and grade averages), so many pages take only a few minutes.

WHAT YOU'LL DO, PER PAGE

1. Try the calculator with a few normal and edge-case inputs and check the answers, including rounding and units.

2. Check the formula shown on the page and the worked examples. Many of these calculators (especially geometry) also show a step-by-step solution and a labelled diagram; check that the steps are mathematically correct and clearly explained.

3. Fill in a short review sheet (we provide it, pre-filled with every page): approved / approved with changes / not approved, with the specific correction. We fix what you flag, you re-check those pages once and give written sign-off.

REQUIREMENTS

- A degree in mathematics, statistics or a related field, and teaching, tutoring or applied-statistics experience. Please mention your qualification in your proposal.

- Fluent written English and a careful eye for detail.

- Consent to be credited publicly: your name, photo, credentials and a short bio on our Reviewers page (https://keencalculator.com/reviewers/) and a "Reviewed by" line with the review date on each page you approve.

LINK AND CREDIT REQUIREMENTS (part of the contract)

- After sign-off, add "Math Reviewer, KeenCalculator.com" to LinkedIn as a Projects or Experience entry, with a link to https://keencalculator.com/.

- Publish one short LinkedIn post about the review, in your own words, with a link to https://keencalculator.com/, disclosed as paid work (for example "paid project").

- If you have a personal or professional website or bio page, add a link to https://keencalculator.com/ there.

- Do this within 7 days of sign-off and keep it live for at least 12 months. In return we link your credit on our site to your LinkedIn or website. Please confirm in your proposal that you're comfortable with this.

BUDGET AND TIMELINE

- $200 fixed price for all 109 pages, including one round of re-checks.

- Review delivered within 3 weeks of the contract start; sending the sheet back one category at a time is welcome.

- More paid review work on new calculators if it goes well.

TO APPLY

Start your proposal with "KEEN-MATH", then give your qualification, and one sentence on a mistake you often see in online math calculators.

nTo qualify for the position of Supervisory Survey Statistician, at GS-1530-12, you must meet the basic qualification requirements listed below.

n

nBasic Education Requirement

nA. Degree: that included 15 semester hours in statistics (or in mathematics and statistics, provided at least 6 semester hours were in statistics), and 9 additional semester hours in one or more of the following: physical or biological sciences, medicine, education, or engineering; or in the social sciences including demography, history, economics, social welfare, geography, international relations, social or cultural anthropology, health sociology, political science, public administration, psychology, etc. Credit toward meeting statistical course requirements should be given for courses in which 50 percent of the course content appears to be statistical methods, e.g., courses that included studies in research methods in psychology or economics such as tests and measurements or business cycles, or courses in methods of processing mass statistical data such as tabulating methods or electronic data processing.

n

n

nB. A combination of education and experience -- courses as shown in A above, plus appropriate experience or additional education. The experience should have included a full range of professional statistical work such as (a) sampling, (b) collecting, computing, and analyzing statistical data, and (c) applying statistical techniques such as measurement of central tendency, dispersion, skewness, sampling error, simple and multiple correlation, analysis of variance, and tests of significance.n

n

nSpecialized Experience: For the GS-12, in addition to meeting the above basic education requirements, you must have one year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the next lower grade level in the Federal service. AtriCure, Inc. provides innovative technologies for the treatment of Afib and related conditions. Afib affects more than 33 million people worldwide.
